text: As Ice Cream melts, it becomes significantly less valuable. If you depend on Ice Cream, keep an eye out for its replacement. Try not to add editions to it, as you'll lose them when it melts away.

name: Invisible Joker
text: Any deck can benefit from Invisible Joker, but the Black Deck offers more rooms to maneuver thanks to its +1 Joker Slot. That said, having an extra joker slot makes Invisible Joker less likely to pick a specific joker.

name: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker does not synergize with any poker hand.

name: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker does not synergize with any other Joker, other than whatever joker you have that's the "best". To provide the best result, players are advised to sell any unimportant Jokers they don't want before selling Invisible Joker, to ensure they get a duplicate of the intended Joker.

name: Invisible Joker
text: Because Verdant Leaf requires selling one Joker to neutralize its effect, Invisible Joker can benefit players if carried from the start of Ante 8, which can then be sold to disable Verdant Leaf and still retain 5 Jokers.

name: Invisible Joker
text: On a Knife's Edge Deck: Invisible Joker might duplicate the Eternal, Pinned Ceremonial Dagger, leaving one permanently stuck behind the other and thus unable to scale.

name: Invisible Joker
text: Generally, passive effect Joker like Four Fingers or Pareidolia do not benefit from being copied by Invisible Joker.

name: Invisible Joker
text: There are also some Jokers that might be expected to work well when copied but can behave unexpectedly with multiple copies. This includes:

name: Invisible Joker
text: Sixth Sense: Only one Spectral card will be created, even with multiple copies of it.

name: Invisible Joker
text: To Do List: Unlike Jokers like Mail-In Rebate, where multiple copies will always choose the same rank, multiple copies of To Do List may want different hands to be played.

name: Invisible Joker
text: Vampire: Only the leftmost Vampire will sca

name: Invisible Joker
text: Unlocking Invisible Joker is done easiest on the Painted Deck since it has -1 Joker slot, but only if the player does not purchase any Negative Jokers, or the Antimatter Voucher.

name: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker can duplicate a second Invisible Joker if players manage to acquire one via Showman. However, the duplicated Invisible Joker will have its rounds played status reset to 0/2.

name: Invisible Joker
text: An Invisible Joker that is duplicated by the Ankh Spectral card will be created with the same number of "round played" status as the original. Any copies created by selling a second Invisible Joker will still have 0/2 rounds played, however.

name: Invisible Joker
text: A duplicated Joker from a Negative edition Invisible Joker can let the player have 1 more Joker than the number of slots. If the player manages to acquire a negative Invisible Joker and sell it with all joker slots filled, the player will still gain a copy of a random joker. Doing so, however, will add -1 to the Joker Slots (example: 6/5), preventing other Negative Jokers from being bought.

name: Invisible Joker
text: If Invisible Joker copies a debuffed Joker, the copied Joker will also be debuffed. The same applies for temporary debuff caused by Crimson Heart, while in next hand they will both recover.

name: Invisible Joker
text: Specifically, if an Invisible Joker copies a debuffed Negative Joker (whether it obtains negative earlier and then debuff, or vice versa), though the copied Joker does not have a negative effect, sell

name: Joker
text: In spite of its pitiful Mult bonus, Joker is a deceptively strong pickup in the early Antes due to its nature as an unconditional and extremely cheap score booster. It doubles the score of the most common 5-card hands at Level 1 (Straight, Flush, and Full House), making it so that every Blind in Ante 1 can be cleared with just one of these hands, provided the base Chips add up to 75 or more. Assuming the player spends $2 in the first Shop to buy Joker, buys/sells nothing else, and scores a sufficient 5-card hand (or Four of a Kind) in all three Blinds without using any more hands, they would enter Ante 2 with a minimum of:

name: Joker
text: $19 on Black Deck

name: Joker
text: $27 on Blue Deck

name: Joker
text: $29 on Green Deck

name: Joker
text: $40 on Yellow Deck

name: Joker
text: $23 on all other Decks

name: Joker
text: While Ante 1 can be cleared without sp

name: Joker Stencil
text: Black Deck is good with this Joker, as this deck gives +1 Joker slot, which basically gives it an extra X1 Mult.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Similarly, Five-Card Draw Deck is even better with this Joker, as this deck gives +2 Joker slots, which basically gives it an extra X2 Mult.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Ghost Deck can be potent with Joker Stencil thanks to its easier access to Spectral cards, especially those mentioned in the Synergetic Spectral cards section.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Nebula Deck is really good with this Joker, as it relies less on having many Jokers, thus freeing up slots.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Zodiac Deck can be good with this Joker, as it gives more chances for cards other than Jokers to appear.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Strong five-card hands like Flush, Straight, or Full House synergize well with Joker Stencil thanks to their high base Mult.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Any Negative Joker works well with this, as they do not take up a Joker slot.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Because the Joker Stencil counts itself as an empty slot, multiple Joker Stencils combine brilliantly. If you have five slots, two Joker Stencils, and no other Jokers, they both provide X5 Mult for a combined total of X25 Mult. A negative joker stencil gives an extra X1 Mult to each Joker Stencil (the formula being X Mult = Empty Joker slots + # of Joker Stencils).

name: Joker Stencil
text: Invisible Joker can be very good for duplicating the Joker Stencil, provided you can play around the loss of X1 Mult for two rounds b

name: Joker Stencil
text: Painted Deck hamstrings Joker Stencil with its -1 Joker Slot, giving it X1 Mult less.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Similarly, Cruelty Deck hamstrings Joker Stencil even more with its -2 Joker Slots, giving it X2 Mult less.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Plasma Deck is also generally not good with this Joker, as usually the player either wants a lot of chips for early antes or needs a lot more mult for later antes, more than what this Joker gives.

name: Joker Stencil
text: 15 Minute City Deck and Blast Off Deck do not work well with Joker Stencil, as these decks both start with two Eternal Jokers, which means Joker Stencil gives less XMult than usual. Not only that, but Blast Off Deck also reduces a Joker slot, which means Joker Stencil gives even less XMult than usual.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Typecast Deck sets your Joker Slots to 0 after ante 4, which sets Joker Stencil to X0 Mult or less.

name: Joker Stencil
text: Weak

name: Jolly Joker
text: Virtually all of the Decks work comparably well with Jolly Joker, as Pair is the easiest hand to assemble - barring High Card (which always is assembled), and it is all but guaranteed to find one after a discard or two outside of the most extreme circumstances.

name: Jolly Joker
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck: These Deck are favored by this Joker, as they contain less overall ranks, and total cards, which makes it that much easier to find a Pair.

name: Jolly Joker
text: Nebula Deck: Scaling Mercury using this Deck's integral Telescope Voucher can make it a worthwhile choice.

name: Jolly Joker
text: Plasma Deck: Has very slight anti-synergy with this Joker, as Additive Mult is overall not a good complement to the Deck's strength; Chips are preferred in the non-Endless Antes, and past that, several sources of Multiplicative Mult are preferred.

name: Jolly Joker
text: Jolly Joker can trigger on any hand except for High Card. Through deck manipulation, even Flushes can benefit. Straight Flushes can benefit under very specific cases when combined with Four Fingers; Straight can benefit under similar circumstances if these two Jokers are also combined with Splash, although this is a highly impractical combo and should be avoided.

name: Jolly Joker
text: Sly Joker and The Duo pair well with this, as both will trigger on the same activation as this joker.

name: Jolly Joker
text: Half Joker can be easily triggered along with this jok

name: Juggler
text: Juggler synergizes with all decks, as +1 hand size is always useful. It is somewhat less useful on Painted Deck, however, due to the missing Joker Slot and that this deck already increases hand size.

name: Juggler
text: Any strong 5 card hands can benefit from Juggler, as the increased hand size means higher chance to draw needed cards to form the hand.

name: Juggler
text: Juggler can also be good in High-card builds which rely on cards being in hand to score, such as with Steel cards.

name: Juggler
text: Baron: gives X Mult for kings held in hand.

name: Juggler
text: Shoot the Moon: gives +13 Mult for each queen held in hand.

name: Juggler
text: Mime: more cards held in hand means more cards for Mime to retrigger.

name: Juggler
text: Reserved Parking: has a 1 in 2 chance to give $1 for every face card held in hand.

name: Juggler
text: Troubadour: +2 hand size, coupled with Juggler, will provide a whooping 11 cards in hand.

name: Juggler
text: Merry Andy: Juggler can offset its -1 hand size penalty.

name: Juggler
text: Stuntman: Juggler can partially offset its -2 hand size penalty.

name: Juggler
text: If Crimson Heart disables Juggler, the hand size will return to normal but current hand will stay intact until the next discard (ex: 9/8). By quitting to Main Menu and returning, the hand size actually permanently increases (ex: 9/9), giving players a permanent hand size upgrade.

name: Juggler
text: The Manacle gets countered by Juggler.

name: Juggler
text: Blackboard can be harder to trigger, as the increased hand size can make it harder to hold only Clubs and Spades in your hand.

name: Juggler
text: The increase hand size will make it hard for Raised Fist to give more score from high-ranked cards.

name: Juggler
text: The Five-Card Draw Deck challenge bans Juggler.

name: Loyalty Card
text: Blue Deck works well with this Joker, as the +1 hand makes it easier to activate.

name: Loyalty Card
text: Any poker hand can benefit from Loyalty Card, but it tends to work best with large hands like Straight and Full House since they tend to struggle against more boss blinds than smaller hands, e.g. The Water, The House, The Fish and The Mouth, and their higher power compensates for Loyalty Card’s long downtime.

name: Loyalty Card
text: Burglar's +3 hands usually allow Loyalty Card to trigger every blind.

name: Loyalty Card
text: The Order, The Trio and Flower Pot provide X Mult that can be triggered every round, and appreciate Loyalty Card's ability to blow through boss blinds like The Water and The House that make the hands necessary to trigger them harder to assemble.

name: Loyalty Card
text: Bloodstone, Smiley Face, Hiker, and all other Jokers that trigger on playing cards appreciate Loyalty Card defeating boss blinds that debuff the required playing cards, like The Head, The Plant, and especially The Pillar.

name: Loyalty Card
text: Grabber and Nacho Tong give you extra hands per round, helping you trigger this more often. With Nacho Tong (or Grabber + Blue Deck), Loyalty Card can trigger every blind if the player opts to use every hand for it, making it significantly stronger.

name: Loyalty Card
text: This Joker is easy to locate when playing a

name: Loyalty Card
text: Black Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Golden Needle Deck all have anti-synergy with Loyalty Card due to their reduced number of hands.

name: Loyalty Card
text: Troubadour has anti-synergy with Loyalty Card, as the -1 hand each round makes it difficult to reach the 6 hands requirement to activate Loyalty Card.

name: Loyalty Card
text: Hieroglyph has anti-synergy with Loyalty Card, as the -1 hand each round makes it difficult to reach the 6 hands requirement to activate Loyalty Card.

name: Loyalty Card
text: The "critical hit" nature of Loyalty Card makes it suitable for dealing with Boss Blinds that punish multiple plays (The Needle, The Tooth, The Eye, or The Fish) and blinds with high score requirements (The Wall and Violet Vessel), as long as it triggers at the appropriate time. Therefore, with Loyalty Card, sometimes it is not better to play fewer hands in a round, but rather to adjust the hands played so that the Loyalty Card can be triggered when needed.

name: Luchador
text: Black Deck: The +1 Joker slot makes carrying this Joker less taxing, as it can be played alongside 5 scoring Jokers. The much less forgiving economy of this Deck in the early game also gives many more opportunities for this card to keep a run alive, allowing for proper capitalization on the benefits of an extra Joker slot later on.

name: Luchador
text: Magic Deck: If the Judgement Tarot card is discovered early in the run, the two starting copies of The Fool can be used to duplicate them, therefore allowing for a quick replacement of this Joker once its effect is activated.

name: Luchador
text: Ghost Deck: This Deck has easier access to the Wraith Spectral card, which serves as a higher-risk but higher-reward version of the aforementioned Judgement. It can also use its starting Hex card to turn Luchador into scoring assistance, but this should only be done as a last resort.

name: Luchador
text: Luchador doesn't benefit any poker hands directly. However, certain hands can occasionally appreciate the assistance it provides (such as Flush against one of the suit-debuffing Boss Blinds, or, less frequently, a High Card/Pair/Three of a Kind build against The Psychic).

name: Luchador
text: Being a utility Joker, Luchador does not directly synergize with any build. However, it can enable a wealth of Jokers that are otherwise soft or hard countered by specific Boss Blinds, in the event they are encountered.

name: Luchador
text: Painted Deck: This Deck has innate anti-synergy due to the -1 Joker slot penalty, and is generally not worth considering anyway due to the +2 hand size bonus allowing for easier assembly of more potent hands.

name: Luchador
text: This also applies to Blast Off Deck and Cruelty Deck.

name: Luchador
text: Matador cannot earn money from a disabled Boss Blind.

name: Luchador
text: Chicot disables the effect of every Boss Blind while it is held. It is a direct upgrade over Luchador in most cases. Due to the role overlap, these two should not be used together.

name: Luchador
text: Amber Acorn flips and shuffles all Jokers, so the player doesn't know which of their Jokers is Luchador. Trying to pick a Joker to sell could likely result in selling the wrong card by mistake.

name: Luchador
text: If Crimson Heart debuffs this card, it can still be sold, but will not disable the Blind.

name: Luchador
text: In fact, for most runs, players are only vulnerable to 1-2 specific Boss Blinds and one Showdown Blind. In an Ante 8 run, excluding Ante 1 and 2 (at which point a specific gameplay style is unlikely to be formed), the probability of encountering both detrimental Boss Blinds, or a Boss Blind combined with a Showdown Blind is relatively low (both around 6%). Therefore, Luchador is sufficient to handle the risk. However, in endless mode, the player will face many Boss Blinds, so it would be better to have a method that can avoid multiple Boss Blinds (such as Chicot and Director's Cut).

name: Lucky Cat
text: Zodiac Deck starting with Overstock and Tarot Merchant improves the chances of finding The Magician in shop.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Magic Deck starts with two copies of The Fool, increasing the player's initial amount of Lucky cards when finding The Magician.

name: Lucky Cat
text: While Lucky Cat technically affects all hands evenly, five-card hands allow more Lucky cards to be played at once, increasing the potential for a successful trigger, such as:

name: Lucky Cat
text: Straight

name: Lucky Cat
text: Flush

name: Lucky Cat
text: Full House

name: Lucky Cat
text: Oops! All 6s doubles the odds of Lucky cards' effects activating. Three copies will guarantee the Mult activation, and therefore, the Xmult for Lucky Cat.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Splash allows five Lucky cards to be scored in case they can't form a five-card poker hand.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Driver's License may benefit with enough Lucky cards in the Deck to activate its conditional X3 Mult.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Retrigger Jokers are very beneficial, as they increase the odds of a successful trigger, further scaling Lucky Cat.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Hack and Sock and Buskin both retrigger cards of certain ranks.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Seltzer retriggers all cards played for 10 hands.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Dusk retriggers all cards played on the final hand.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Hanging Chad retriggers the first card played twice, benefiting the player as long as the Lucky card is placed first.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Red Seal double the opportunities for the Lucky car

name: Lucky Cat
text: Bram Poker Deck makes Lucky Cat useless due to the Eternal Vampire this deck starts with.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Vampire is not recommended, as it removes the Lucky enhancement when scored, making Lucky Cat impossible to scale.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Midas Mask converts all face cards into Golds, therefore overriding the previous Enhancement.

name: Lucky Cat
text: Vagabond may be risky to use, as just one $20 trigger will prevent it from creating more Tarot cards (unless the player has $-16 or less, which is pretty unlikely).

name: Lucky Cat
text: The Pillar debuffs previously played cards of the Ante, which may make some Lucky cards unusable.

name: Lucky Cat
text: The Fish can potentially make it hard to play hands with Lucky cards if multiple hands are required to defeat the Boss Blind.

name: Lusty Joker
text: Magic Deck's Fool Tarots can be used to mass-convert cards to have Heart suits.

name: Lusty Joker
text: Ghost Deck can find a Sigil Spectral card in the shop, which may convert cards into Hearts.

name: Lusty Joker
text: This Joker is easier to take with Checkered Deck, as the deck starts with 26 Heart playing cards.

name: Lusty Joker
text: This Joker works best with Flush-type hands that only contain Hearts:

name: Lusty Joker
text: Flush

name: Lusty Joker
text: Straight Flush (and Royal Flush)

name: Lusty Joker
text: Flush House

name: Lusty Joker
text: Flush Five

name: Lusty Joker
text: Other hands that score more cards are generally better to play with Lusty Joker, as they allow more Heart cards to be scored.

name: Lusty Joker
text: As Lusty Joker's effect triggers when a Heart card is scored, retrigger Jokers, that allow cards to be scored multiple times, are very good to combo with Lusty.

name: Lusty Joker
text: Flush Jokers, like Crafty Joker and Droll Joker, work well with Lusty Joker, as you want to be playing flushes to maximize Lusty's effect anyways.

name: Lusty Joker
text: Bloodstone also triggers off of Heart cards scored, forming a natural synergy with Lusty Joker. As Bloodstone gives X Mult on a chance basis, Lusty Joker can be a natural addition to Oops! All 6s builds, which tend to use Lucky cards and other chance-based Joker effects, or other "X Mult from cards played" Jokers, like The Idol or, sometimes, Ancient Joker.

name: Lusty Joker
text: Because Lusty Joker's Mult is applied during the scoring of your played cards, Jokers that focus on creating Tarot cards are helpful to Lu

name: Lusty Joker
text: When facing The Head, all Heart cards are debuffed, meaning Lusty Joker cannot activate.

name: Mad Joker
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck work well with this Joker thanks to their smaller deck, allowing you to find a Two Pair easier.

name: Mad Joker
text: Erratic Deck can work well with this Joker if it randomizes a lot of cards with the same rank.

name: Mad Joker
text: Any Poker Hand that contains a Two Pair will benefit from Mad Joker. These are:

name: Mad Joker
text: Two Pair

name: Mad Joker
text: Full House

name: Mad Joker
text: Flush House

name: Mad Joker
text: Flush - only if the flush contains a Two Pair

name: Mad Joker
text: Four of a Kind and similar hands do not trigger Mad Joker.

name: Mad Joker
text: Spare Trousers gains Mult when playing a Two Pair.

name: Mad Joker
text: Square Joker gains Chips any time a played hand consists of exactly 4 cards. Since a standard Two Pair is exactly four cards, the player can strengthen Square Joker while getting Mult from Mad Joker.

name: Mad Joker
text: Sly Joker and Clever Joker give Chips on a Pair and Two Pair respectively.

name: Mad Joker
text: Jolly Joker gives Mult if the played hand contains a Pair.

name: Madness
text: Madness adds multiplicative Mult at a prodigious rate, but the player will need more than multiplicative Mult to win a run. For that reason, it's best to choose decks that can feasibly feed into Madness from an early point.

name: Madness
text: Ghost Deck on some occasions, can be potent with Madness. If the player is playing on Black Stake or above and Madness is Eternal, the player can safely use the given Hex to give it Polychrome or even Ankh it to create multiple copies of Madness that cannot destroy each other, scaling the player's scoring power at an astounding rate.

name: Madness
text: On occasions where the player opts for a Madness-only Joker run, Painted Deck and Cruelty Deck may feasibly work well, as their reduced Joker slots are rendered moot in most cases.

name: Madness
text: Non-Perishable Deck works well with Madness, as all Jokers are Eternal, and Madness cannot destroy them but is still able to scale.

name: Madness
text: Typecast Deck might work well with Madness, as after defeating Ante 4's boss, all Jokers will become Eternal, allowing Madness to scale freely without destroying other Jokers.

name: Madness
text: Some Challenge Decks that start with Eternal Jokers, such as 15 Minute City Deck, Bram Poker Deck, Blast Off Deck, etc., may work well with Madness.

name: Madness
text: Madness synergizes poorly with hands that have low native Mult and rely on Jokers for bonuses, but quite well with hands that have high

name: Madness
text: Anaglyph Deck has slight anti-synergy with this Joker, as it encourages the player to skip blinds, which remove an opportunity to scale Madness.

name: Madness
text: On Plasma Deck the player nearly always wants to take advantage of the easy early Antes by using a few chips Jokers and as many value generators as possible. However, taking Madness early makes it very difficult to do so, as well as preventing the player from pivoting their Chips to Mult if they took any Eternal Jokers.

name: Madness
text: Any Joker that cannot receive the Eternal sticker is inherently anti-synergistic with Madness, such as Gros Michel, as it has the potential to be destroyed before the player can get full value from the Joker.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Red Deck grants an extra discard, allowing more cards of the selected rank to be discarded.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Painted Deck allows the player to have more cards in hand, letting the player discard more cards without sacrificing good hands.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Black Deck can more easily take Mail-In Rebate, as it has more Joker slots, and it is recommended to discard more with Black Deck anyway, as the player must play better hands to compensate for having fewer hands. Black Deck can also hold more Jokers that help with discarding, like Drunkard.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck both contain fewer ranks and total cards, making it easier to find the selected rank and discard it.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Golden Needle Deck removes money when discarding, and Mail-In Rebate is an effective counter to this.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Hands that need fewer cards are better if the player has a smaller hand size, like Three of a Kind, which allows them to discard 5 cards if they have the default hand size. For this reason, Straight, Flush, and Full House are less valuable with Rebate.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: However, Five of a Kind and Flush Five are sometimes better in highly centralized decks, as with more of that rank, Mail-In Rebate will likely choose that rank, and discarding them will be fine, as the player is more likely to draw more to form a Five of a Kind still.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Blast Off Deck doesn't work well with Mail-In Rebate, as this deck only starts with 2 discards.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Any Jokers that benefits from not using Discards, like Delayed Gratification or Banner, have anti-synergy with Mail-In Rebate.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Burglar removes all discards, effectively disabling Mail-In Rebate.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: The Water sets your discards to 0, making Mail-In Rebate useless for the round.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Since debuffed cards do not have a rank, any blind that debuffs cards makes it less likely for the player to make use of Mail-In Rebate.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Blue Stake and above hinder Mail-In Rebate's potential because they have 1 less discard by default.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate has an extremely high potential cash output. The player should try and maximize its potential by ensuring that all the cards in your deck are the same rank. This can be done through a variety of methods.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Copying Mail-In Rebate with Blueprint or Brainstorm while discarding 5 cards gives a total of $50, and adding more copies just adds more money per discard.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: The player should be careful not to discard too much, as completely running out of cards is an instant loss.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate has an extremely high potential cash output. The player should try and maximize its potential by ensuring that all the cards in your deck are the same rank. This can be done through a variety of methods.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: Copying Mail-In Rebate with Blueprint or Brainstorm while discarding 5 cards gives a total of $50, and adding more copies just adds more money per discard.

name: Mail-In Rebate
text: The player should be careful not to discard too much, as completely running out of cards is an instant loss.

name: Marble Joker
text: Plasma Deck can use the Stones created to great effect. Marble's Stone cards could win the entire run in combination with only a few other Chip Jokers and/or Planet cards.

name: Marble Joker
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck have fewer cards than other decks, meaning the player will be able to draw a mixture of Stone and non-Stone cards more consistently.

name: Marble Joker
text: Red Deck allows you to find Stone cards easier, letting the player play more hands with as many Stone cards as possible.

name: Marble Joker
text: Blue Deck's extra hand allows the player to play more Stone card hands and scale hand-based mult-scaling Jokers.

name: Marble Joker
text: Black Deck's extra Joker slot makes it easier to take Marble, as there will be more Jokers to carry it as it starts to create Stone cards.

name: Marble Joker
text: High Card is the best hand to use with Stone cards, as you can end up playing five of them. Besides that, Pair and Three of a Kind still allow you to play a few Stone cards, and Two Pair and Four of a Kind allow you to play one. Straight, Flush, and Straight Flush can also be played with one stone card with Four Fingers. No other hand can be played with Stone cards. You will want to end up focusing on High Card, as it is the most reliable and plays the most Stone cards.

name: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker will only work with some way to scale Mult. This can be scaling based on hands played, like from Ride the Bus or Supernova, scaling

name: Marble Joker
text: If Marble Joker is held for a long time or is Eternal, higher value poker hands like Straight and Four of a Kind that rely on finding specific cards are much harder to find with many Stones in the deck.

name: Marble Joker
text: Erosion relies on a small deck size, which is more difficult to get when 1 card is added per round from Marble Joker.

name: Marble Joker
text: Since the Stone cards given by Marble Joker always score no matter what, Splash becomes unnecessary.

name: Marble Joker
text: Generally, Marble Joker isn't a strong Joker. Stones only really work with High Card and Pair builds, and you need a large amount of them in your deck to consistently draw and play them. Marble Joker ends up in an awkward state early where it takes up a Joker slot that could be used for another Chips provider like Stuntman or Castle that can work better with High Card builds. However, the Stone cards it adds can end up supplanting a Chips Joker entirely, meaning you can sell Marble after getting value from it and go into the final Boss Blind with an extra Mult or effect Joker you'd be missing otherwise. With that said, Marble joker can be great when it's fueling some specific other jokers.

name: Matador
text: Matador gains the most value out of being used during applicable Boss Blinds the most amount of times. This generally means you want more hands, and Blind reroll abilities if the boss won't trigger Matador.

name: Matador
text: Blue Deck allows you to play more hands, allowing Matador to trigger more often.

name: Matador
text: Anaglyph Deck appreciates a way to make money that isn't hindered by needing to play Blinds instead of skipping them.

name: Matador
text: Double or Nothing Deck will trigger Matador when attempting to score debuffed cards, even during Small and Big Blinds.

name: Matador
text: Burglar is the best Joker to combine Matador with, as with ideal draws you can obtain an additional $24 from each Boss Blind.

name: Matador
text: To the Moon can benefit from the mid-round money earning, as this money will count toward interest.

name: Matador
text: Jokers such as Bull or Bootstraps that directly scale off of money enjoy the extra cash that Matador brings in.

name: Matador
text: Jokers such as Flash Card or Red Card that scale off of actions that require money to be spent can also benefit from the extra spendable cash.

name: Matador
text: Mr. Bones makes Matador less punishing.

name: Matador
text: Using Pareidolia during The Plant will debuff every single card, which means playing any hand will always trigger Matador.

name: Matador
text: Similarly, using Smeared Joker during any of the four suit-debuffing Boss Blinds will double the amount of cards debuffed, doubling the chances for Matador to trigger.

name: Matador

name: Matador
text: Black Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Golden Needle Deck don't allow the player many chances for Matador to trigger due to their reduced number of hands.

name: Matador
text: Checkered Deck starts with 0 Clubs and 0 Diamonds in the deck, which makes it significantly harder for the player to earn money when playing against The Club or The Window.

name: Matador
text: Abandoned Deck and Medusa Deck start with no face cards, meaning the player will struggle to make use of Matador if the upcoming Blind is The Plant.

name: Matador
text: Boss-Blind-disabling Jokers like Luchador and Chicot should generally be treated as mutually exclusive with Matador, as their abilities to disable Boss Blinds' abilities leave Matador useless.

name: Matador
text: Matador only triggers if the debuffed card is played and "scored". This means e.g. a High Card with one non-debuffed scoring card and some debuffed cards that do not "score" will not trigger Matador.

name: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy is a good Joker early game for the economy of the Green Deck, since it gains no interest and instead earns money only based on discards and hands remaining, extra discards are pretty valuable. Merry Andy can also be useful early game for the Painted Deck, as its hand size penalty is completely negated by the Painted Deck's bonus hand size.

name: Merry Andy
text: Straights usually require more discards to set up.

name: Merry Andy
text: If the player needs to draw a specific enhanced card to win, Merry Andy enables the player to sift through up to 15 more cards every round.

name: Merry Andy
text: Although, the reduced Hand Size makes it harder to hold multiple Steels and Golds at once.

name: Merry Andy
text: Juggler helps with negating this Joker's downside.

name: Merry Andy
text: Banner can combo with Merry Andy to provide additional chips early game.

name: Merry Andy
text: Castle and Yorick can scale much faster since Merry Andy allows you to discard 15 more cards per blind.

name: Merry Andy
text: It also works well with Delayed Gratification for economy, increasing the payout by an extra $6. However, the smaller hand size will make it harder to play certain hands.

name: Merry Andy
text: Blackboard benefits from reduced hand size, making it easier to hold only Spades or Clubs for its Mult bonus.

name: Merry Andy
text: Raised Fist becomes easier to use with high-ranked cards.

name: Merry Andy
text: Paint Brush and Palette can mitigate Merry Andy's -1 hand size penalty.

name: Merry Andy
text: Five-Card Draw Deck's reduced hand size may make it impossible to play certain poker hands.

name: Merry Andy
text: Jokers with held in hand abilities vary with Merry Andy's effectiveness.

name: Merry Andy
text: Baron, Shoot the Moon, and Reserved Parking are all weakened due to holding fewer face cards in hand.

name: Merry Andy
text: Inversely, Raised Fist actually benefits, as the player is less likely to hold a card with a low rank at any moment.

name: Merry Andy
text: Burglar always removes all discards, effectively making Merry Andy -1 Hand Size with no upside.

name: Merry Andy
text: Stuntman adds an additional -2 hand size, making it difficult to feasibly form 5-card poker hands.

name: Merry Andy
text: Green Joker and Ramen discourage discarding due to weakening with each used discard.

name: Merry Andy
text: Ectoplasm should not be used more than once with Merry Andy, as its permanent hand size reduction can make even han

name: Merry Andy
text: As skipping is usually a high-risk strategy, it can be tricky to win a run in 12 or fewer rounds, meaning the player must skip at least 12 Blinds, averaging at 1.5 Blinds per Ante skipped.

text: Plasma Deck can skip more in the early game due to its balancing ability, making the need to obtain Jokers early less of a priority.

name: Merry Andy

name: Merry Andy
text: Tags in general to look out for are Investment Tag and Speed Tag, as earning Economy is critical since the player sees fewer Shops and Blind payouts overall.

name: Midas Mask
text: Mad World Deck starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which makes it so that all cards are upgraded to Gold cards when scored.

name: Midas Mask
text: Any five-card hand with five face cards will benefit Midas Mask the most. This includes Flush, Full House, Five of a Kind, Flush House, and Flush Five.

name: Midas Mask
text: Since it is slightly more difficult to make a Straight or Straight Flush with face cards than other cards, Midas Mask is slightly less useful if you have invested in those hands.

name: Midas Mask
text: Late game, playing small hands like High Card means you can keep more Gold cards in hand.

name: Midas Mask
text: Mime means the Gold cards make twice as much money.

name: Midas Mask
text: Midas Mask naturally synergizes with Smiley Face, Scary Face, and Business Card when playing the face cards. However, you're not going to want to play your golden face cards later in the game.

name: Midas Mask
text: It has an extremely strong synergy with Pareidolia, which makes it so that all cards are upgraded to Gold cards when scored.

name: Midas Mask
text: Beware of using Stones with this strategy, as they will also be turned into regular Gold cards, which may ruin a run based on Stone cards.

name: Midas Mask
text: Golden Ticket makes Gold cards give +$4 when played.

name: Midas Mask
text: Vampire removes card enhancements in exchange for X0.1 Mult per enhancement removed, making it a potent combination with Midas

name: Midas Mask
text: This Joker is close to useless on the Abandoned Deck and Medusa Deck since it has no face cards.

name: Midas Mask
text: The Plant debuffs all face cards, preventing Midas Mask from making any gold cards for the round.

name: Midas Mask
text: The Fragile Deck challenge bans Midas Mask.

name: Mime
text: The Painted Deck gives an additional +2 to the player's hand size, allowing Mime to activate more cards.

name: Mime
text: The Ghost Deck allows for Spectral cards to be readily available in the Shop, making Seals more attainable.

name: Mime
text: High Card is arguably the best hand with Mime, since it requires the least amount of cards to play. This allows for more cards to be held in hand.

name: Mime
text: Pair and Three of a Kind can be used for the same reasons, although slightly less effectively.

name: Mime
text: Held in hand Jokers synergize the best with Mime, since it enables them to be activated twice. These include:

name: Mime
text: Reserved Parking will generally give $0.25 more on average.

name: Mime
text: This can change depending on retriggers and held in hand effects, see the Reserved Parking page for an explanation on the specific interactions and numbers.

name: Mime
text: Raised Fist and Shoot the Moon: Provides double their + Mult to the score.

name: Mime
text: Baron: Potentially the strongest duo with Mime by giving an additional X1.5 Mult for each retrigger. This, paired with the Plasma Deck, can also allow the player to possibly reach the elusive Naneinf score.

name: Mime
text: Steel Joker: Steels are exceptionally strong with Mime, and attaining more Steel cards will also scale this Joker.

name: Mime
text: Constellation: Blue Seals are retriggered by Mime, creating more planets and scaling this Joker faster.

name: Mime
text: Medusa Deck can be difficult to use with Mime due to the Eternal Marble Joker adding more Stones to the deck, making finding cards that Mime works with more difficult.

name: Mime
text: Five-Card Draw Deck does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers, though it can still be used with Raised Fist.

name: Mime
text: Mime suffers from Jokers that reduce hand size, such as Stuntman and Merry Andy, due to them lowering the number of cards with "Held in Hand" abilities able to be active at once.

name: Mime
text: Notably, Mime does not affect Blackboard despite its ability having the "held in hand" description.

name: Mime
text: Golden Ticket encourages the player to play Gold cards instead of keeping them in hand, making Mime weaker.

name: Misprint
text: Blue Deck: +1 hand per round means one more opportunity for Misprint to save the run with a high roll.

name: Misprint
text: This Joker provides unconditional +Mult, so it works for all played hands. Hands with low Mult at base and low Mult from levelling, such as High Card, Pair, and Two Pair, benefit from +Mult sources more than faster scaling hands such as Straight and Four of a Kind.

name: Misprint
text: Multiple Misprints, or Misprint copied with Blueprint/Brainstorm: The Mult given by these jokers will be generated independently, which reduces the randomness of the total Mult.Mathematically, this is called a uniform sum distribution or Irwin Hall distribution, see Irwin-Hall Distribution for details.

name: Misprint
text: Grabber and Nacho Tong each give +1 hand per round, which means one more opportunity for Misprint to save the run with a high roll. This is especially valuable earlier on.

name: Misprint
text: Painted Deck: This Deck should avoid Misprint outside of absolute emergencies; consistency is the key to making the most out of a Joker roster that is one slot short.

name: Misprint
text: Golden Needle Deck makes it very risky to use Misprint because this deck only has 1 hand, which mean scoring too little at any point will lead to game over.

name: Misprint
text: The average Mult added by Misprint is +11.5 Mult, which is statistically better on paper than other Common +Mult Jokers (Joker, Jolly Joker, Mad Joker, and Droll Joker to name a few). This and the unconditionality of Misprint make it very suitable for the early stage of a run, when the player lacks powerful Jokers and specific gameplay style—for example, it is possible for Misprint to give +23 Mult, which is roughly equivalent to X6.75 Mult even for the high hands (Straight, Flush, or Full House), if the player does not have any other Mult Jokers or hand upgrades.

name: Misprint
text: However, due to randomness of Misprint, it is hard to rely on it for scoring. In later stages of a run, Misprint is very replaceable in favor of Specialized Additive Mult Jokers, such as Fibonacci or Onyx Agate, or ones capable of very fast scaling, such as Red Card or Spare Trousers, based on the play style of this run.

name: Misprint
text: Also, in a 'sink or swim' scenario where the player needs a consistent source of scoring, a Joker that provides less +Mult on average but has a lower capacity to low roll may be favorable.

name: Misprint
text: Both low rolls and high rolls from Misprint can be harmful; a low roll can lead to you not scoring enough to beat a blind, and while a high roll may enable you to beat a blind with fewer hands, it can also hinder scaling hand-based Jokers like Green Joker and Square Joker as a result.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Black Deck gives 1 extra Joker slot in exchange for 1 fewer hand, which can be used by Mr. Bones, as 1 less hand makes it harder to get to the required score.

name: Mr. Bones
text: This Joker does not affect any poker hand but may be slightly more useful for certain builds.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Showman can let the player pick up multiple Mr. Bones, which they would likely need the effects of due to missing 3 scoring Jokers by that point.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Blueprint and Brainstorm can't copy this Joker, so don't try to get multiple extra lives out of it.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Matador becomes less punishing with Mr. Bones. This can be useful for the player to get a lot of money with little to no consequences.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Being saved by Mr. Bones will still award the player a win on Ante 8, effectively making this joker divide the final round's chip requirement by 4. Note that being saved by this Joker will not allow it to gain a stake sticker.

name: Mr. Bones
text: If Mr. Bones gets debuffed on the final hand of Crimson Heart, it will not save the player.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones can be useful when the play style of a round is extremely fragile to certain Boss Blinds, for example:

name: Mr. Bones
text: With a deck mostly consisting of a certain suit, or with Smeared Joker: The Club, The Goad, The Window, and The Head.

name: Mr. Bones
text: With a deck mostly consisting of face cards, or with Pareidolia: The Plant, The Mark.

name: Mr. Bones
text: With a high-leveled hand: The Flint.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Relying on a certain hand type, or with Card Sharp: The Eye and The Arm.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Relying on using discards to build hands: The Wheel, The Water, Cerulean Bell.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Relying on combination of all held Jokers: Verdant Leaf, Crimson Heart.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Relying on good economy: The Ox and The Tooth.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Relying on hands that are hard to play, or with Burglar: The Mouth and The Fish.

name: Mr. Bones
text: Being relatively weak and relying on multiple hands to defeat blinds: The Needle, The Wall, and Violet Vessel.

name: Mr. Bones
text: With a big hand size: The House.

name: Mr. Bones
text: In fact, for most runs, players are only vulnerable to 1-2 specific Boss Blinds and one Showdown Blind. In an Ante 8 run, excluding Ante 1 and 2 (at which point a specific gameplay style is unlikely to be formed), the probability of encountering both detrimental Boss Blinds, or a Bo

name: Mystic Summit
text: Burglar is a good combination with Mystic Summit, as it trades all discards for +3 hands. This allows Mystic Summit to be in effect as soon as the round starts.

name: Mystic Summit
text: If the player is able to find Yorick, Mystic Summit is a great choice as both incentivize using all of the player's discards. In addition, Mystic Summit provides + Mult to be boosted by Yorick's X Mult.

name: Mystic Summit
text: Mystic Summit has anti-synergy with the Green Deck, since one of the ways to get money with the Green Deck is to retain discards, and Mystic Summit is only effective when all discards are gone.

name: Mystic Summit
text: Golden Needle Deck removes $1 for every discard used, which means Mystic Summit costs $6 to activate during this challenge.

name: Mystic Summit
text: Five-Card Draw Deck has a hand size of 5, which might force the player to discard a wanted card to activate Mystic Summit.

name: Mystic Summit
text: Green Joker and Ramen are likely a bad choice, due to having to spend discards for Mystic Summit. This can be mitigated with Burglar but as this combo requires three Jokers it may be best to ignore it.

name: Mystic Summit
text: Any Joker that benefits from retaining discards, such as Banner or Delayed Gratification are not a good combination with Mystic Summit.

name: Obelisk
text: Red Deck's extra discards, Painted Deck's higher hand size, and Abandoned Deck's smaller deck size all allow the player to find more unique hands, which helps with keeping the X Mult on Obelisk without risking playing the most played hand. Painted Deck also appreciates having such a high-value X Mult Joker.

name: Obelisk
text: Blue Deck's extra hands allow Obelisk to scale faster per round.

name: Obelisk
text: Checkered Deck makes Flush easier to play, as the deck only has Spades and Hearts. Using this deck allows another option for the most played hand type other than Pair and Two Pair to build around and then pivot out of. It also helps the player after pivoting if the build does not revolve around Flush beforehand, as having another hand type that's easy to hit reduces the chance of resetting Obelisk accidentally.

name: Obelisk
text: No particular poker hand is better with Obelisk. The Pair or Two Pair strategy mentioned below could be considered a synergy, but the bulk of the game will be spent playing as many different hands as possible to keep options open in the future.

name: Obelisk
text: Jokers that produce Mult without hand-based conditions are what you always want to use with Obelisk. These can be flat + Mult Jokers, like Fibonacci and Gros Michel, but the most success comes from scaling ones, like Bootstraps, Erosion, Ride the Bus, or Fortune Teller. Having one of these scaling Jokers

name: Obelisk
text: Black Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Golden Needle Deck all have poor synergy with Obelisk due to their reduced number of hands.

name: Obelisk
text: Nebula Deck has slight anti-synergy with Obelisk, as Telescope encourages building around a single most-played hand type, which Obelisk discourages.

name: Obelisk
text: Burglar removes all discards and may force the most played hand to be played, resetting Obelisk.

name: Obelisk
text: All Jokers that rely on playing specific hands, including Superposition, Crazy Joker, and The Order, will not be able to be used as much.

name: Obelisk
text: Planet cards and Jokers that upgrade hands, like Space Joker and Burnt Joker, are far less effective because the hand can only be used a limited number of times.

name: Obelisk
text: Telescope encourages focusing on a single poker hand, which is the opposite of what Obelisk needs to scale.

name: Obelisk
text: Obelisk can become a very powerful Scaling X Mult Joker, but it cannot be used in every build. It works best on builds that don't rely on playing specific hands to score, as if too many of any one hand are played, you can no longer play it without resetting the Obelisk.

name: Obelisk
text: The most effective strategy with Obelisk is to play Pair or Two Pair until around 15 have been played, then pivoting in the later antes to playing any other hand. It is not recommended to use Obelisk if the most played hand is High Card, as the player runs a higher risk of being forced to reset the Obelisk.

name: Odd Todd
text: Red Deck's extra discard makes finding strong hands with many odd ranks easier.

name: Odd Todd
text: Abandoned Deck works best with Odd Todd thanks to having no face cards, allowing players to find odd ranks easier.

name: Odd Todd
text: Mad World Deck will also work as well, although this deck doesn't start with any Aces.

name: Odd Todd
text: Magic Deck's Fool Tarots can be used as Strengths, converting even ranks or Kings into odd ranks.

name: Odd Todd
text: Plasma Deck can use the large influx of Chips to win a large number of early hands, allowing one to search for better Jokers easier.

name: Odd Todd
text: Any poker hand can benefit from Odd Todd provided it is comprised of mainly odd cards. Todd works the best with five-card hands that encourage repeating ranks, like Full House and Five of a Kind.

name: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd generates +155 Chips when five odd ranks are scored, and more if any of those cards retrigger. This amount of Chips encourages taking more + Mult and X Mult Jokers to balance Chips and Mult. Many of them work well, though notable ones include Fibonacci and Scholar, as both also trigger on certain odd ranks.

name: Odd Todd
text: Retrigger effects increase the amount of Chips Odd Todd produces. Notably, Hack works very well, as it offers unconditional retriggers on Threes and Fives (which also are triggered by Fibonacci).

name: Odd Todd
text: Cloud 9 scales its money generation off having more Nines in your deck. These Nines become better to play with Odd Todd's extra chips.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Playing any Flush-type hand full of Clubs will benefit greatly from Onyx Agate, those being:

name: Onyx Agate
text: Flush

name: Onyx Agate
text: Straight Flush

name: Onyx Agate
text: Flush House

name: Onyx Agate
text: Flush Five

name: Onyx Agate
text: Gluttonous Joker also triggers when Club cards are played, though the bonus is strictly inferior.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Smeared Joker allows Spade suit to benefit from Onyx Agate as well.

name: Onyx Agate
text: In this context, Arrowhead can be a substantial addition as the player will gain both Chips and Mult.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Blackboard can be an easy addition, as if the player as the deck set up to have a lot of Clubs, Blackboard will benefit too.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Retrigger Jokers work very well with Onyx Agate, as the extra triggers adds more Mult, on top of other card Enhancements that could benefit scoring power.

name: Onyx Agate
text: For a Flush build, The Tribe will capitalize on Onyx Agate's Mult bonus.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Photograph can work reasonably well as long as the face card is placed to the far right, activating its XMult after Onyx Agate's Additive Mult.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Wilds count as Clubs, which will activate Onyx Agate's Mult bonus.

name: Onyx Agate
text: As Onyx Agate already provides a hefty Mult bonus, Bonuss fit quite nicely to double as a source of Chips.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Glasss may be the most potent synergy as it directly synergizes with Onyx Agate's Additive Mult, however, there is always the risk of the Glass breaking.

name: Onyx Agate

name: Onyx Agate
text: The Checkered Deck cannot benefit from Onyx Agate due to lack of Clubs, unless combined with the Smeared Joker.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Seeing Double will only activate if a Club and another suit score, rendering it useless for Flush builds which is where Onyx Agate shines best.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Although, the bonus may still be activated if a Wild card is used.

name: Onyx Agate
text: While Four Fingers can make Flushes easier to play, it enables the player to do so with less overall cards, therefore the scoring power of Onyx Agate is weakened if the player opts for a 4-card Club Flush.

name: Onyx Agate
text: It may be suitable to hunt for Planet cards and/or scaling Chip Jokers if Four Fingers must remain in conjunction with Onyx Agate.

name: Onyx Agate
text: When facing The Club, all Club cards are debuffed, meaning Onyx Agate cannot activate.

name: Onyx Agate
text: The Pillar may be problematic as previously played Club ca

name: Onyx Agate
text: Unlike unlocking Arrowhead and Bloodstone, fulfilling the condition of 30 Club cards in a Deck is trickier, as it doesn't allow for an easy strategy such as using the Checkered Deck for the aforementioned Jokers.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Magic Deck starts the player with two copies of The Fool, allowing for easier Deck manipulation early on by finding The Moon or Death.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Any Jokers that synergize with Flush builds are likely to be useful during the unlock attempt, such as Droll Joker, Crafty Joker, and The Tribe.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Economy Jokers are likely to be beneficial to find more Tarots for Deck manipulation, such as Mail-In Rebate and Golden Joker.

name: Onyx Agate
text: Non-club Wilds or Spades cards with Smeared Joker do not count towards Onyx Agate's unlock condition.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: This Joker benefits Jokers that have probability effects:

name: Oops! All 6s
text: 8 Ball's effect becomes a 2 in 4 chance to generate a Tarot card when an 8 is scored.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Space Joker's effect becomes a 2 in 4 chance to upgrade any hand when played.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Reserved Parking and Business Card become guaranteed to give money on held face cards and scored face cards respectively.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Hallucination guarantees a tarot card when opening a booster pack.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Bloodstone becomes guaranteed to apply its multiplier effect.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Gros Michel's chance of extinction increases to a 2 in 6 chance, which can speed up the process of having one break to spawn a Cavendish.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: This comes at the downside of an increased risk to lose out on +15 Mult.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s can also benefit Jokers that indirectly use probability effects:

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Lucky Cat can scale faster, as Luckys have an increased chance to trigger.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Glass Joker, Canio, and Erosion can scale faster due to the increased chance of Glasss breaking.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s's effect stacks with multiple copies of itself. With two copies of Oops! All 6s, probabilities are effectively quadrupled. For example, The Wheel of Fortune will always trigger, and Glasss will always break when played. Oops! All 6s is incompatible with Blueprint and Brainstorm, but multiple copies can be obtained in normal play

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Painted Deck, Blast Off Deck and Cruelty Deck reduce the amount of Joker Slots, which makes it less convenient to use Oops! All 6s.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Driver's License can suffer slightly from Glass cards' increased chance of destruction, but it also benefits from Lucky Cards increased chance of triggering, especially the Mult chance.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: Cavendish's chance to destroy itself is doubled to a 2 in 1000 chance.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: While the increased chance of Glass breaking is beneficial for deck thinning, it also can pose an issue if they are crucial for survival.

name: Oops! All 6s
text: The Wheel will have an increased chance of flipped cards, becoming 2 in 7. With 3 copies of Oops! All 6s, this chance is increased to 8 in 7, causing all playing cards to be drawn face

name: Oops! All 6s
text: The Fragile Deck challenge starts the player with two Eternal Negative copies of Eternal Oops! All 6s, while all cards are Glasss.

name: Pareidolia
text: Black Deck: This deck provides an extra Joker slot, making it easier to work with Pareidolia since it does not directly improve the player's build, without having other face card orientated Jokers to leverage it.

name: Pareidolia
text: Abandoned Deck: Potentially benefits from having Pareidolia by giving access to face card bolstering Jokers.

name: Pareidolia
text: A larger poker hand is generally more ideal to play, since it can trigger more Jokers that trigger off of face cards, including Four of a Kind, Full House, Flush, etc..

name: Pareidolia
text: The type of poker hand it is counted as is unaffected by the played cards counting as "face cards", since Pareidolia does not change a rank or suit.

name: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia also lets Stones be treated as face cards, thus able to work with effects triggered from face cards.

name: Pareidolia
text: Because Pareidolia does not change the rank of the card (rather, it just makes all playing cards count as face cards), it does not interfere with the effects of Jokers like Fibonacci which trigger on specific ranks.

name: Pareidolia
text: Generally, Pareidolia has synergy with any Joker that is triggered from face cards. Some specific Jokers it works well with include:

name: Pareidolia
text: Avoid this Joker on the Painted Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Cruelty Deck, as their inherent reduced Joker slots makes Pareidolia extremely hard to use without going out of your way to hold more Jokers or scale certain poker hands with Planet cards.

name: Pareidolia
text: Ride the Bus will reset back to +0 Mult on every hand played when Pareidolia is present.

name: Pareidolia
text: There is one Boss Blind that weakens Pareidolia-based builds, and another that is extremely run-threatening:

name: Pareidolia
text: The Mark: All cards are drawn face-down, making it far more difficult to assemble a sufficiently-scoring hand. This can be somewhat remedied by carrying Enhancing or Suit-changing Tarot cards into this Boss Blind, allowing a few cards to be identified at a time. Similarly, and more effectively, albeit much rarer, the Ouija and Sigil Spectra

name: Pareidolia
text: The Mad World Deck challenge starts the player with an Eternal, Negative copy of Eternal Pareidolia.

name: Perkeo
text: Having access to many consumables is one of the most important aspects when owning Perkeo, as it grants a wider selection of choices for Perkeo to duplicate, allowing the player to make better decisions depending on what they can get it to copy. Perkeo fits well in any deck, but notable standouts are:

name: Perkeo
text: Ghost Deck is undoubtedly the deck that works best with Perkeo, as Spectral cards are, by nature, a huge game-changer due to their drastic effects at various degrees. The ability to buy Spectral cards directly from the Shop can be unfathomably powerful, allowing the player to create copies of powerhouses like Cryptid to duplicate powerful cards, or the likes of Deja Vu and Aura to enhance existing cards in their deck. Without it, the only way to get Spectral cards into the consumable slots to copy will be Séance or Sixth Sense, which is way harder to make use of.

name: Perkeo
text: Zodiac Deck due to the increased consumable rate in the Shop coming from both the Tarot Merchant and Planet Merchant vouchers, as well as easier access to their upgrades, Tarot Tycoon and Planet Tycoon, and just more shop items in general thanks to the Overstock voucher, and again, easier access to its upgraded version, the Overstock Plus voucher.

name: Perkeo
text: Perkeo can benefit any unlocked poker hand equally. Acquiring the desired poker hand's Planet and keeping it in the consumable slo

name: Perkeo
text: Painted Deck can be harder to utilize due to its -1 Joker slot penalty, since Perkeo generally provides no direct benefits for scoring. In most cases this isn't really an issue though, as the benefits that Perkeo provides generally far outweigh the downside.

name: Perkeo
text: Madness should not be used, since Perkeo is a Legendary and therefore cannot have an Eternal sticker outside of challenge decks.

name: Photograph
text: The Ghost Deck can be a good choice since it gives easier access to Deja Vu for Red Seal, and Familiar for more face cards.

name: Photograph
text: Full House, Two Pair, Straight, and Flush are the best early game, as they give additional opportunity for Enhanced and/or Edition Aces and numbered cards to activate their effects first. Additionally, all of these except Two Pair have relatively high starting raw Mult stats, enabling more benefit from Photograph's xMult early on.

name: Photograph
text: Straight, Four of a Kind, and Secret Hands are the best late game, as the high base Mult from Saturn, Mars, and the Secret Hand Planet cards far outscale any + Mult effects.

name: Photograph
text: Hanging Chad: Popularly known together as "Photochad", these are one of the most reliable duos in the game, with a powerful early game combo that has the potential to stay relevant in the late game. Due to their low rarity, it makes it easy to create this pair with a low total cost of $9, providing X8 Mult and +20 Chips on their own if the first scored card in a hand is a face card.

name: Photograph
text: For example: A Flush will score a minimum of 2,528 (Fa 5 4 3 2), a Full House 2,752 (Fa Fa 2 2 2), and a Straight 3,008 (J 10 9 8 7). This means, with a little luck, Ante 2 on any Stake can be cleared in a single hand pe

name: Photograph
text: Abandoned Deck and Medusa Deck should not be used with Photograph, as they have no face cards by default. A possible exception is if Pareidolia is used alongside.

name: Photograph
text: Faceless Joker incentivizes discarding face cards, making it harder to preserve one for Photograph.

name: Photograph
text: Ride the Bus: As scoring a face card resets it back to +0 Mult, this Joker is unable to use its own effect without decimating many rounds' worth of Additive Mult scaling.

name: Photograph
text: Canio encourages the player to destroy face cards, which doesn't work well with Photograph.

name: Photograph
text: The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Photograph useless.

name: Photograph
text: The Mark may be an issue if your poker hand relies on particular ranks, such as Straights.

name: Popcorn
text: Any deck can benefit from Popcorn. However, Plasma Deck benefits the least due to its balancing feature, where Chips are better than Mult.

name: Popcorn
text: Any poker hand can benefit from Popcorn.

name: Popcorn
text: Throwback benefits Popcorn the most, as it gets stronger when skipping blinds, allowing Popcorn to stay alive for more rounds.

name: Popcorn
text: The Non-Perishable Deck challenge bans Popcorn.

name: Raised Fist
text: Five-Card Draw Deck's reduced hand size makes it easier to hold only high-ranked cards.

name: Raised Fist
text: High Card and Pair allow playing low-value cards without forcing them to be part of the scoring hand.

name: Raised Fist
text: Baron multiplies the Mult from Raised Fist if the lowest card is positioned to the left of any held Kings.

name: Raised Fist
text: Mime retriggers Raised Fist because its ability activates on cards held in hand.

name: Raised Fist
text: Stuntman shrinks hand size, making it easier to hold only high-ranked cards, and provides extra Chips to pair with Raised Fist's Mult.

name: Raised Fist
text: Merry Andy also reduces hand size for better card control and offers more discards to remove low-ranked cards.

name: Raised Fist
text: Steels multiplies the Mult from Raised Fist if the lowest card is placed to the left of any Steel cards in hand.

name: Raised Fist
text: If the lowest-ranked card itself is Steel, the X1.5 Mult multiplier applies first, which actually results in a lower total score.

name: Raised Fist
text: Red Seals will retrigger Raised Fist if it activates on a card with a Red Seal.

name: Raised Fist
text: Strength can be used to raise card ranks.

name: Raised Fist
text: The Hanged Man can remove lower-ranked cards completely, making higher ranks more likely to appear in hand.

name: Raised Fist
text: Death can transform low-ranked cards into higher ones.

name: Raised Fist
text: The Chariot can turn some cards into Steel cards, which can multiply Raised Fist's Mult.

name: Raised Fist
text: Painted Deck's larger hand size can make it difficult to hold only high-ranked cards.

name: Raised Fist
text: Five-card hands like Straight and Full House make it harder to control what's left in hand, since no extra non-scoring cards can be included.

name: Raised Fist
text: Juggler, Troubadour, and Turtle Bean increase hand size, with which holding only high-ranked cards becomes harder.

name: Raised Fist
text: Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can make holding only high-ranked cards harder.

name: Raised Fist
text: In case there are multiple lowest-rank card held in hand, Raised Fist triggers on the rightmost card with that rank.

name: Raised Fist
text: Because the cards held in hand can be moved around before pressing play, any held cards with an X Mult multiplier should be placed to the right of the lowest-ranked card(s) to get the most value. Similarly, if the player holds multiple cards of the lowest rank, and one is debuffed or has a Red Seal, placing the stronger card to the right will yield a better score.

name: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist provides +0 Mult for debuffed cards.

name: Raised Fist
text: Stones do not have a rank and can never trigger Raised Fist.

name: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist does not give extra Mult from cards upgraded by Hiker.

name: Ramen
text: Green Deck: Perhaps the most obvious synergy exists with this Deck; conserving discards for money gives a mild source of income to compensate for the extra hands required to capitalize on Ramen's power.

name: Ramen
text: Blue Deck: The extra hand every round makes it less punishing to play 'throwaway' hands as makeshift discards that also ease a bit of scoring tension, which better preserves this Joker's power.

name: Ramen
text: Nebula Deck: With Ramen skewed more towards easier-to-find hands in desperate need of scaling, the built-in Telescope Voucher this Deck provides makes it a natural choice.

name: Ramen
text: All Decks with consistency-based bonuses allow them to form better hands in the absence of discards, which helps make much more out of Ramen than usual. These include the Painted Deck (+2 hand size), the Checkered Deck (only Hearts and Spades), and especially the Abandoned Deck (no face cards), which can very easily leverage the fast scaling of Straights with the Saturn Planet card in tandem with this Joker. Even certain Erratic Deck seeds can lend themselves well to consistently finding high-performing hands.

name: Ramen
text: This Joker works best with weaker hands that can be more reliably made without discarding (or by using a hand as a makeshift discard), such as High Card, Pair, Two Pair, and Three of a Kind. To that end, this will force the player to become more dependent on Planet card scaling than wit

name: Ramen
text: Red Deck: This Deck has anti-synergy with this Joker, as it encourages the player to discard more to find better hands.

name: Ramen
text: Black Deck makes it very difficult to use Ramen, as it suffers from -1 hand per round. This forces more dependency on discards while disallowing liberal use of 'throwaway' hands.

name: Ramen
text: Similarly, Blast Off Deck makes it even more difficult to use Ramen, as this deck only has 2 hands. This forces much more dependency on discards while disallowing liberal use of 'throwaway' hands.

name: Ramen
text: Golden Needle Deck starts with only one hand and 3 extra discards, which means Ramen will rarely see its full value in this deck.

name: Ramen
text: Drunkard and Merry Andy: The extra discards these two provide are almost useless in a Ramen build, except when considering the potential presence of Banner or Delayed Gratification. Using 3 Joker slots for such

name: Ramen
text: The Non-Perishable Deck challenge bans Ramen.

name: Red Card
text: Anaglyph Deck can build up many tags, then copy any tag that gives a Mega Booster Pack.

name: Red Card
text: Green Deck encourages the player to spend money as they earn it, which works well with Red Card.

name: Red Card
text: In Typecast Deck, after Ante 4, Buffoon Packs will continue to spawn in the shop despite it being impossible to take Jokers from them. Red Card can be used to extract value from what would otherwise be a wasted booster slot.

name: Red Card
text: Red Card synergizes well with most economy Jokers that provide money, like Business Card or Rocket.

name: Red Card
text: Astronomer can provide free Celestial Packs that can be used to scale.

name: Red Card
text: Hallucination can allow you to still get tarot cards even while skipping packs.

name: Red Card
text: Clearance Sale and Liquidation lower the price of booster packs, making it easier to purchase and skip more.

name: Red Card
text: Hieroglyph and Petroglyph send the player back an Ante at the cost of -1 Hand and -1 Discard respectively, allowing them to open more booster packs to skip.

name: Red Card
text: Skipping for these Tags works best when the player is on the Anaglyph Deck or has taken lots of Diet Colas.

name: Red Card
text: Standard Tag, Charm Tag, Meteor Tag and Buffoon Tag all give access to Mega Booster Packs, which can be used by taking 1 card, then skipping to scale Red Card.

name: Red Card
text: Ethereal Tag gives access to a Spectral Pack, which can optionally be skipped to scale Red Card.

name: Red Card
text: There are a lot of Jokers that, when combined with Red Card, leave the player in a dilemma between whether to scale Red Card or whether to scale the other joker. However, it is worth emphasizing again that skipping a Booster Pack specifically to scale up Red Card (instead of skipping a Booster Pack that already had very little value) might not be a good idea. Moreover, it is debatable whether these are true anti-synergies (rather than complements), since pairing the Red Card with any of these lessens the punishment of opening Booster Packs that don't have what you want:

name: Red Card
text: Jokers that care about Tarot cards, such as Fortune Teller, Driver's License, and Vampire.

name: Red Card
text: Jokers such as Steel Joker and Lucky Cat, which care about specific Tarot cards.

name: Red Card
text: Jokers that care about Planet cards, such as Constellation and Satellite.

name: Red Card
text: As for Standard Pack

name: Red Card
text: When playing with Red Card, it's better not to skip Booster Packs specifically just to scale the Red Card. Opening a Booster Pack is more like rolling for a chance to get a good item — Booster Packs are not guaranteed to provide value, and the player would skip many Booster Packs anyway due to not getting a card that is sufficiently valuable. What Red Card does is that it provides +3 Mult in all of the cases where the player would have skipped anyway, so it is better to think of Red Card as an additional Booster Pack slot and to only skip if none of the options are better than +3 mult.

name: Red Card
text: For instance, with 9 Planet cards available at the beginning of a run and three of those being visible in a regular Celestial Pack, assuming no Telescope, there is only a 1 in 3 chance for a Celestial Pack to contain the Planet card that one actually wants. The other two-thirds of the time, the player would just skip or take a Planet card of an undesirable hand, gaining little to no value out of it. But with the Red Card, the player would get a minimum of +3 Mult — it might be more reasonable to think of it as a fourth Planet card that gives +3 Mult for every hand (assuming no X Mult triggered on played or held cards).

name: Red Card
text: If the player opens a Mega Booster Pack, the player can still use the first card and then skip to scale up Red Card.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Painted Deck's larger hand size potentially allows for Reserved Parking to activate more often.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Blue Deck’s extra hand allows for more hands that can be used to yield money and dig for face cards.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Mad World Deck starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which makes it so that all cards are considered face cards, causing Reserved Parking to potentially activate on all cards held in hand.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Since it's best to keep as many face cards in hand as possible, smaller hands like High Card and Pair work well.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Oops! All 6s guarantees that Reserved Parking will trigger.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Mime retriggers all card held in abilities, including Reserved Parking’s effect.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Pareidolia makes it so that all cards are considered face cards, causing Reserved Parking to potentially activate on all cards held in hand.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Shoot the Moon also wants the player to keep face cards (Queen) in hand.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Baron also wants the player to keep face cards (King) in hand.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Ride the Bus also does not want to play face cards. Note that having these 2 jokers at the same time can be very dangerous, as there's a small chance of drawing a hand of only face cards.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Juggler and Troubadour increase hand size, allowing the player to hold more cards in hand.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Burglar gives 3 extra hands, allowing more chances for Reserved Parking to give more money.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Abandoned Deck and Medusa Deck start with no face cards, meaning Reserved Parking Joker is useless.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Black Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Golden Needle Deck all have fewer hands to be used for yielding money.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Five-Card Draw Deck does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Five-card hands like Flush, Straight or Full House leaves fewer cards held in hand so it doesn't benefit Reserved Parking much.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Merry Andy and Stuntman reduce hand sizes, which means the player hold less face cards.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Faceless Joker encourages discarding lots of face cards.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Canio encourages destroying face cards.

name: Reserved Parking
text: Business Card encourages playing face cards instead, although this could actually be a synergy if the player has a lot of face cards

name: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking rolls a 1 in 2 on each face card held in hand, so the expected value per face card per hand is $0.5. Mime and Red Seal will only attempt to retrigger this effect if the initial roll was successful. As a result, one retrigger will raise the expected value to $0.75 per card per hand, and two retriggers raises the expected value to $1.

name: Reserved Parking
text: If the player also already has another held in hand effect that triggers on every hand, like Baron, Shoot the Moon or Steels, then Mime and Red Seal will always retrigger this effect, and therefore this card. As a result, Reserved Parking can be retriggered even if the initial roll was unsuccessful. In this case, one retrigger raises expected value to $1 per hand, two retriggers raises expected value to $1.5.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Abandoned Deck and Medusa Deck start with no face cards, so this Joker will almost never reset.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Blue Deck gives +1 hands every round, allowing for more scaling per round.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Any hand will work with this Joker. However, the smaller the hand type, the better Ride the Bus is. This makes it ideal for High Card or Pair builds, while Straights and Flushes builds can be more difficult.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Jokers whose effects trigger based on numbered cards can be more useful, such as Even Steven, Odd Todd, Fibonacci, and Hack.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Canio scales greatly from destroying face cards, thus both thinning the deck and providing a significant X Mult to complement the additive Mult of Ride the Bus.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Though, Canio encourages adding face cards to the deck in order to destroy them, which can make it harder to work around Ride the Bus.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Trading Card can destroy face cards, making it easier for the player to avoid resetting Ride the Bus.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Burglar adds 3 extra hands and removes all discards, allowing Ride The Bus to scale faster.

name: Ride the Bus
text: However, missing out on discards can be dangerous, as the player might be forced to reset Ride The Bus. It is especially important to remove face cards from the deck when running Burglar and Ride the Bus.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Black Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Golden Needle Deck all have poor synergy with Ride the Bus due to their number of reduced hands.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Mad World Deck doesn't work with Ride the Bus, as this Deck starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which means Ride the Bus will never scale or gain + Mult.

name: Ride the Bus
text: X-ray Vision Deck randomly flips cards, which can cause players to accidentally play a face card.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Pareidolia will ruin Ride the Bus' multiplier as soon as any hand is played.

name: Ride the Bus
text: Splash can trigger a face card that otherwise would have done nothing.

name: Ride the Bus
text: The following Jokers' effects rely on scoring face cards, meaning they cannot be utilized without resetting Ride the Bus.

text: Business Card

name: Ride the Bus
