name: Riff-Raff
text: Black Deck works well with Riff-Raff, as it gives an additional Joker slot at the cost of losing a hand.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Similarly, Five-Card Draw Deck works even better with Riff-Raff, as it gives two additional Joker slots at the cost of only having a hand size of 5.

name: Riff-Raff
text: On a Knife's Edge Deck starts with an Eternal, Pinned Ceremonial Dagger, which means Riff-Raff can provide disposable Jokers to feed the Dagger. Make sure to keep a disposable Joker in between them so Riff-Raff can be kept after selecting a blind.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Since Riff-Raff is a utility Joker, it does not have specific synergy with any hand.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Ceremonial Dagger: By providing free fodder to feed it, this Joker can scale its +Mult much more reliably.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Campfire: Similarly, having free Jokers to sell allows Campfire to scale easily.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Abstract Joker: Riff-Raff ensures the player's Joker slots are filled, so it makes it easy to get +Mult for Abstract Joker.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Gros Michel: If the player is lucky enough to get this Joker from Riff-Raff, it can be a good way to get the powerful Cavendish later.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Due to the random nature of Riff-Raff, it has the potential to either have great or poor synergy with the player's other Jokers depending on what Common Jokers it provides.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Purchasing Blank and then Antimatter gives the player an

name: Riff-Raff
text: Painted Deck reduces Joker slots by one, making it harder to have extra space for Riff-Raff to spawn Jokers.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Similarly, Cruelty Deck reduces Joker slots by two, making it even harder to have extra space for Riff-Raff to spawn Jokers.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Non-Perishable Deck makes it very risky to use Riff-Raff, as it spawns Eternal Common Jokers on this deck.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Joker Stencil: Since Riff-Raff constantly adds Jokers, it reduces the X Mult it can get.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Swashbuckler: Common Jokers generally don't have a high selling value, so they will add less +Mult to Swashbuckler.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Baseball Card: This Joker only scales its X Mult from owning Uncommon Jokers, meaning the Jokers provided by Riff-Raff are useless to it.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Notable interactions with other Jokers/game mechanics include:

name: Riff-Raff
text: Jokers generated by Riff-Raff can potentially come with Editions, including Negative.

name: Riff-Raff
text: When playing on higher Stakes, Riff-Raff will not create Jokers with in-run Stickers, such as the Rental sticker.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Jokers generated during the Non-Perishable Deck will still receive an Eternal sticker.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff is able to spawn Cavendish as long as Gros Michel went extinct (destroyed itself) earlier in the run.

name: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff can create Jokers that are undiscovered in the player's collection.

name: Riff-Raff
text: When the player possesses Showman, Riff-Raff can create a second Riff-Raff.

name: Riff-Raff
text: If all Joker slots are currently filled when the Blind is selected, and then Ceremonial Dagger consumes a Joker, Riff-Raff will create another Joker, as long as it's on the right of Ceremonial Dagger.

name: Riff-Raff
text: If all Joker slots are currently filled when the Blind is selected, and either Ceremonial Dagger or Madness destroys a Negative Joker, Riff-Raff will be able to create a non-Negative Joker. This is similar to selling a Negative Invisible Joker, which leads to a -1 Joker Slot situation.

name: Rocket
text: Bootstraps increases its Mult provided as players have more money.

name: Rocket
text: Bull increases its Chips provided as players have more money.

name: Rocket
text: Painted Deck and Cruelty Deck: The reduced Joker slots makes it difficult to carry Rocket since players may need more scoring Jokers to survive and beat Ante 8.

name: Rocket
text: Anaglyph Deck: As the player ideally wants to avoid skipping to make use of Rocket's payout at the end of the round, this Deck has a slight anti-synergy with it.

name: Rocket
text: Throwback: Skipping Blinds is less than ideal for most Economy Jokers, to which Rocket is no exception.

name: Rocket
text: If Crimson Heart disables Rocket upon playing a winning hand, it will not gain $2 nor any accumulated money upon cashing out.

name: Rocket
text: The increment for defeating a Boss Blind is added before it pays out for the end of that round.

name: Rocket
text: The Omelette Deck challenge bans Rocket.

name: Rocket
text: The Blast Off Deck challenge starts the player with an Eternal copy of Rocket.

text: Unlike unlocking Arrowhead and Bloodstone, fulfilling the condition of 30 Diamond cards in a Deck is trickier, as it doesn't allow for an easy strategy such as using the Checkered Deck for the aforementioned Jokers.

name: Rough Gem
text: Magic Deck starts the player with two copies of The Fool, allowing for easier Deck manipulation early on by finding The Star or Death.

name: Runner
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck both have fewer cards than the standard Deck, making it easier to locate specific cards for Straights.

name: Runner
text: Painted Deck with its increased Hand Size, can make Straights easier to form with more cards held in hand.

name: Runner

text: 15 Minute City Deck starts with an Eternal Shortcut, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand.

name: Runner
text: Straight, Straight Flush, and Royal Flush are recommended to scale Runner consistently.

name: Runner
text: Shortcut allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand.

name: Runner
text: Four Fingers allows Straights to be scored with only four cards instead of the usual five, making it easier to get that hand.

text: Ectoplasm and Ouija have anti-synergy with Runner, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but Ouija converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights less consistent.

name: Satellite
text: Checkered Deck works well with Satellite as it requires fewer Deck modifications to unlock the secret Poker hands.

name: Satellite
text: Erratic Deck may require no Deck modifications at all to unlock the secret Poker hands.

name: Satellite
text: Playing the three secret hands (Flush House, Five of a Kind and Flush Five) to unlock their planets allows players to maximize this Joker's value.

name: Satellite
text: Since Satellite is maximized through the use of Planet cards, it synergizes with Constellation, which gains X0.1 Mult per planet card used.

name: Satellite
text: Satellite benefits from Astronomer, which makes planet cards and Celestial booster packs free.

name: Satellite
text: Smeared Joker can make it much easier to unlock the secret hands, thereby maximizing Satellite's value.

name: Satellite
text: The High Priestess can potentially spawn Planet cards not yet used by the player if found early, boosting Satellite.

name: Satellite
text: Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon increase the frequency of planet cards in the shop, making it easier to find different planet cards.

name: Satellite
text: Showman can have anti-synergy with Satellite, since it will allow duplicate planet cards to appear, and Satellite requires unique planet cards.

name: Satellite
text: Telescope can make it harder to achieve max rewards with Satellite, as it lends itself to the same planet card repeating.

name: Satellite
text: This innately applies to the Nebula Deck as it starts with the Telescope Voucher.

name: Satellite
text: Without a steady Economy, unlocking Satellite may prove to be a difficult task.

name: Satellite
text: The Yellow Deck is a decent choice for the run to unlock Satellite as it starts the player with an extra $10, earning the player Interest from defeating the first Blind of the run, and setting up for further Economic gain.

name: Satellite
text: Economy Jokers such as Golden Joker, Mail-In Rebate, etc. are directly helpful in reaching the unlock condition.

name: Satellite
text: The Bull and Bootstraps Jokers both gain scoring power relative to the player's Money, which would be useful to have in a run that attempts to unlock Satellite as hoarding Money to reach $400 will also give it scoring power.

name: Satellite
text: Egg and Gift Card add sell value, making it possible to hold onto the Egg or a useless Joker/Consumable to sell later for a substantial boost in Money.

name: Satellite
text: Swashbuckler would quantify the sell value into Mult, which may help the player continue the run.

name: Satellite
text: To the Moon, Seed Money, and Money Tree allow the player to earn more Interest, which may contribute to reaching the unlock condition faster.

name: Satellite
text: All 3 of these combined allow for the player to earn a maximum of $40 from Interest alone, merely one-tenth of the required amount.

name: Satellite
text: The Omelette Deck challenge bans Satellite.

name: Scary Face
text: Red Deck’s extra discard can be used to dig for more face cards in the player’s deck.

name: Scary Face
text: Painted Deck has a larger hand size, allowing for more face cards to appear. However, the -1 Joker slot means Scary Face may not be as viable as some other options.

name: Scary Face
text: Plasma Deck can use the large influx of Chips to win a large number of early hands, allowing one to search for better Jokers easier.

name: Scary Face
text: Mad World Deck starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which causes Scary Face to trigger on all played cards.

name: Scary Face
text: Scary Face requires face cards (King, Queen, and Jack) to trigger, so hands with more face cards in them will allow Scary Face to award more Chips. For example, a Full House consisting of K K K Q Q will trigger Scary Face five times.

name: Scary Face
text: If the first card of the hand is a face card, Hanging Chad will cause Scary Face to trigger thrice, giving +90 Chips.

name: Scary Face
text: Pareidolia causes Scary Face to trigger on all played cards, effectively making every card a Bonus.

name: Scary Face
text: Sock and Buskin will add an additional +30 Chips per face card scored.

name: Scary Face
text: Triboulet provides a Mult multiplier for each played King or Queen.

name: Scary Face
text: Business Card gives each face card played a 50% chance to provide $2 when scored.

name: Scary Face
text: Smiley Face provides additional Mult for each face card played.

name: Scary Face
text: Splash allows non-scoring cards to trigger Scary Face (by maki

name: Scary Face
text: Abandoned Deck and Medusa Deck are not recommended due to lack of face cards.

name: Scary Face
text: Baron, Shoot the Moon, Hit the Road and Reserved Parking encourage not playing face cards.

name: Scary Face
text: Ride the Bus actively punishes playing face cards.

name: Scary Face
text: Canio's ability activates only upon destroying face cards, resulting in fewer cards able to trigger Scary Face.

name: Scary Face
text: The Plant will debuff all face cards, meaning Scary Face Joker cannot trigger.

name: Scholar
text: Abandoned Deck can reliably find Aces more often than the typical 52-card decks.

name: Scholar
text: Red Deck gives +1 discard, allowing for more opportunities to dig for Aces.

name: Scholar
text: Pair of Aces

name: Scholar
text: Three of a Kind with Aces

name: Scholar
text: Four of a Kind with Aces

name: Scholar
text: Five of a Kind with Aces

name: Scholar
text: Flush Five with Aces

name: Scholar
text: Straight or Straight Flush with 5-4-3-2-A or A-K-Q-J-10

name: Scholar
text: Full House with 2 or 3 Aces

name: Scholar
text: Flush House with 2 or 3 Aces

name: Scholar
text: In general, the more Aces you play in a hand, the more valuable Scholar will be.

name: Scholar
text: Fibonacci gives you +8 Mult per Ace.

name: Scholar
text: Odd Todd adds +31 Chips per Ace.

name: Scholar
text: Aces do not have a retrigger Joker associated with their rank. However, Hanging Chad, Dusk and Seltzer (and Sock and Buskin if Pareidolia is owned) can still be used to trigger Aces multiple times.

name: Scholar
text: DNA can copy an Ace every first hand.

name: Scholar
text: Superposition creates a Tarot card if the played hand is a Straight which contains an Ace.

name: Scholar
text: Trading Card can help thin the deck out, so you can draw Aces more reliably.

name: Scholar
text: Any jokers requiring multiples of the same rank cards like The Trio, Zany Joker, etc..

name: Scholar
text: Tarot cards:

name: Scholar
text: The Hanged Man can be used to thin out the deck and make Aces easier to find.

name: Scholar
text: Death can be used to turn other cards into Aces.

name: Scholar
text: Strength can be used to upgrade Kings into Aces.

name: Scholar
text: 15 Minute City Deck and Mad World Deck are not recommended, as these decks don't contain any Aces by default.

name: Seeing Double
text: Erratic Deck may start with more Clubs than a standard deck, and allows for more X of a Kind, like Pair or Three of a Kind, to be played, which could activate Seeing Double's condition more easily.

name: Seeing Double
text: Straight and Full House both generate X2 Mult a large majority of the time, making Seeing Double great for those strategies.

name: Seeing Double
text: Smeared Joker means Clubs can also count as Spades and vice-versa. This means that playing any hand (even High Card) containing a Club or Spade will trigger Seeing Double.

name: Seeing Double
text: This interaction is a bug. This interaction doesn't apply if the card is Wild.

name: Seeing Double
text: Splash allows triggering the bonus by adding an extra card that would otherwise be ineligible for scoring; e.g. ♣️A ♣️A ♣️A ♣️A ♥️4.

name: Seeing Double
text: Almost any hand that triggers Flower Pot will also trigger Seeing Double, providing a total of X6 Mult.

name: Seeing Double
text: If some cards are debuffed, Flower Pot may trigger without Seeing Double, as Seeing Double requires at least 1 non debuffed Clubs and at least 1 non debuffed non Clubs, while Flower Pot still counts debuffed cards.

name: Seeing Double
text: Wilds can count as either the Club or the non-Club, but not both. Generally this means adding any second scoring card (including a second Wild card) will trigger the bonus, though Stones will not qualify, h

name: Seeing Double
text: Checkered Deck makes it significantly harder to activate Seeing Double, as it contains no Club cards naturally.

name: Seeing Double
text: Flush-based hands are hard to use, requiring a Wild, Smeared Joker or an off-suit card via Four Fingers and Splash.

name: Seeing Double
text: The Club renders Seeing Double useless, as all Club cards are debuffed and debuffed Club cards will not trigger Seeing Double.

name: Seeing Double
text: The Pillar can make Seeing Double difficult to trigger if players already played some Club cards in the previous round, making them debuffed upon facing this boss blind. This can be remedied by carrying Tarot cards that provide enhancements into the boss blind to "revive" debuffed Club cards.

name: Seeing Double
text: Unlocking Seeing Double may prove to be challenging at first due to its condition being oddly specific towards a specific rank and suit. In particular, there are no Jokers that directly have synergies with 7s, the sole exception being Odd Todd. Here are some approaches that can help with unlocking Seeing Double:

name: Seeing Double
text: Magic Deck starts with two copies of The Fool, allowing the player to copy Tarots to make more 7 of Clubs, such as Death, The Moon, Strength, or even The Lovers.

name: Seeing Double
text: Erratic Deck can generate with more 7 of Clubs from the start.

name: Seeing Double
text: Wild of any suit and 7s of Spades with Smeared Joker can also be used.

name: Seltzer
text: Zodiac Deck is helpful for finding tarot cards to make the enhanced cards that make Seltzer work effectively.

name: Seltzer
text: Red Deck is able to find better hands on average, so Seltzer will last longer, as less hands need to be played per round.

name: Seltzer
text: Black Deck is able to stack more Jokers that benefit from Seltzer's effect. Adding even a single X Mult Joker like Ancient Joker can be an extra X7.5 Mult normally, but with Seltzer it becomes an extra X57 Mult.

name: Seltzer
text: Plasma Deck gains a huge boost from stacking X Mult modifiers, which Seltzer enables very well.

name: Seltzer
text: Any 5-card hands like Flush, Straight, or Full House will provide more retriggers from Seltzer. In particular, Flush Fives, with five of the same very strong duplicated card, work very well.

name: Seltzer
text: Any Joker that triggers on scoring will have its effect doubled, for instance Scary Face for Chips, Fibonacci for +Mult, The Idol for X Mult, or Rough Gem for money.

name: Seltzer
text: Jokers that scale based on cards played, like Lucky Cat and Hiker, work very well with Seltzer, as the cards they scale with will always retrigger, and the scaling will remain after Seltzer is consumed.

name: Seltzer
text: Jokers like 8 Ball (in particular, due to its on scoring nature) and Cartomancer can provide frequent Tarot cards to buff up playing cards.

name: Seltzer
text: Throwback rewards you for skipping blinds, making Seltze

name: Seltzer
text: Copying cards with DNA will quickly use up Seltzer's retriggers.

name: Seltzer
text: Similarly, destroying 6s with Sixth Sense will also quickly use up Seltzer's retriggers.

name: Seltzer
text: Jokers that incentivize playing many hands per round, such as Green Joker or Vagabond, will similarly cause Seltzer to be spent quickly.

name: Seltzer
text: Using Burglar does not always guarantee winning in one hand, so the player will have to play hands as pseudo-discards, which will quickly deplete Seltzer.

name: Seltzer
text: If a hand that is not allowed is played during The Psychic, The Mouth or The Eye, Seltzer will still lose a retrigger.

name: Seltzer
text: In a build with many enhanced cards, Seltzer can be a powerful joker, especially in the late game. Due to Seltzer's limited lifespan, it is often used to get the highest scoring single hand possible in endless mode.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: The Painted Deck has a larger hand size, making this Joker easier to use.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: All hands that do not use Queens benefit from this Joker.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: In decks with a hand limit of 8 or less, hands that require 5 cards make this Joker more difficult to use. Conversely, smaller hands, such as High Card, can use this Joker effectively every hand.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: This Joker may not be good when trying to make Straights, as the Straight cannot exceed a Jack unless Shortcut is in use.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Mime doubles the trigger of this Joker's effect.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Midas Mask can add a buff to played Queens, providing an additional benefit thereafter when Queens are held in hand.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Reserved Parking provides cash when face cards are held in hand.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Baron increases the amount of Mult gained by X1.5 Mult per held King, which can ride off of Shoot the Moon's Additive Mult for additional value. Shoot the Moon can also be used as a stepping stone for strengthening Queens to Kings for a Baron build.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: As previously mentioned, the player must physically move the Kings to the right of the Queens for maximum scoring value.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Trading Card can remove non-Queen cards, allowing you to see and hold Queens easier.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Death and Strength can turn some cards into Queens.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: The Hanged Man can remove non-Queen cards, allowing you to see and hold Queens easier.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: The Chariot can turn some cards into Steel cards,

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Abandoned Deck, Mad World Deck, and Medusa Deck can be difficult to use, as they naturally contain no Queens.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Five-Card Draw Deck does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, will make the player hold fewer Queens.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: The Hook discards 2 random cards after playing a hand, which may render Shoot the Moon useless if the Queens were discarded.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Queens useless for the round.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: The Mark draws all face cards face down, which makes the player unable to tell which card is a Queen.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Cerulean Bell may force a Queen to be played or discarded.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: Verdant Leaf debuffs all cards, including Queens, until a Joker is sold.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: If the player has any cards in hand that give X1.5 Mult, either Steels or owning a Baron, it is ideal to manually drag the Queens to the far left so as to make Shoot the Moon's +Mult trigger before the X Mult, maximizing the scoring power for the poker hand played. The reason for this is that any held-in-hand abilities are triggered from left to right. Therefore, placing any card far left will prioritize that specific held-in-hand effect. However, when enhancing a Queen itself to be a Steel card, the X Mult will always apply before Shoot the Moon's +Mult.

name: Shoot the Moon
text: The unlock requirement for Shoot the Moon does not necessarily mean to play one card of each rank with the Heart suit, so having just one Heart card in the deck and playing it will unlock Shoot the Moon. A suitable strategy to unlock it is with an Erratic Deck configuration with few Hearts, or Abandoned Deck, since it only has 10 Heart cards. Conversely, it is harder to unlock on Checkered Deck due to the big amount of Heart cards.

name: Shortcut
text: Black Deck: The +1 Joker Slot allows Shortcut to function as a utility Joker while still providing space for 5 other Jokers to score.

name: Shortcut
text: Abandoned Deck lowers the range of card values from A-K to A-10, making it significantly more likely to draw a Straight, especially with Shortcut.

name: Shortcut
text: Checkered Deck in tandem with Shortcut increases the likelihood of finding a playable Straight Flush.

name: Shortcut
text: Straight

name: Shortcut
text: Straight Flush (or Royal Flush)

name: Shortcut
text: Four Fingers is a great combination with Shortcut, as this allows for a 4-length Straight with gaps, and Straight Flushes become even easier to make since the Straight and Flush don't need to be on the same 4 cards. (e.g. Q♠️ J♠️ 9♥️ 7♠️ 3♠️ is a valid Straight Flush with both Jokers in effect)

name: Shortcut
text: Crazy Joker and The Order give additive and multiplicative Mult respectively when a Straight is played.

name: Shortcut
text: Devious Joker and Runner both give Chips when a Straight is played.

name: Shortcut
text: Superposition and Séance create Consumables when a Straight or Straight Flush is played.

name: Shortcut
text: Space Joker and Burnt Joker appreciate Shortcut’s effect allowing for multiple straights to be formed in one round, and can make use of Straights having incredibly strong Planet scaling.

name: Shortcut
text: Obtaining Saturn from cards with a Blue Seal becomes much easier due to the decreased difficulty of forming a straight allowing more discards t

name: Shortcut
text: Mathematically, Shortcut is slightly better than Four Fingers in creating Straights.[https://www.reddit.com/r/balatro/comments/1b68mpp/statistical_analysis_of_the_four_fingers_and/ Statistical Analysis of the "Four Fingers" and "Shortcut" Jokers for Straights], a Reddit post However, Four Fingers is better at helping create Flushes and Straight Flushes. The player can consider choosing between the two, or combining the two to gain more Straights (in which case, Straights are almost always present in the 8 cards), but at the risk of losing two scoring Jokers.

name: Showman
text: Showman is effective with any deck, but is particularly strong on Black Deck due to the +1 Joker slot bonus.

name: Showman
text: Showman has no direct effect on any specific poker hands. It does, however, make Celestial Packs less reliable, as its effect allows them to give duplicate planets. This decreases the chances of a Celestial Pack containing your desired Planet card, as well as preventing Planet Blocking (holding useless Planets in your consumable slots so they can't appear elsewhere) impossible.

name: Showman
text: Showman has no direct Joker synergies. However, its main benefit lies in it being one of very few ways to obtain multiple copies of the same Joker.

name: Showman
text: Cavendish is a powerful common Joker, making it likely to appear again before ante 8.

name: Showman
text: Photograph and Hanging Chad have notable synergy and are also common Jokers, making them appear more often.

name: Showman
text: Blueprint and Brainstorm are strong in long endless runs.

name: Showman
text: The Idol is also powerful in endless runs.

name: Showman
text: Because it allows for duplicated Planet cards to appear, Showman synergizes with the Observatory by allowing for planet cards to appear in the shop whilst they are in the consumable space. However, this is easier achieved with Blue Seal.

name: Showman
text: Showman can also create problems when Telescope is not yet redeemed, as Celestial Packs will often contain multiple copies of irrelevant planet cards.

name: Showman
text: Showman can make The Emperor and Riff-Raff generate themselves.

name: Showman
text: Although the probability is extremely low, Showman can even make multiple copies of The Soul or Black Hole appear in Booster Packs.

name: Showman
text: If the player has Showman and finds a duplicate of any of their Jokers in the shop, if they sell that Joker and replace it with the shop duplicate, (as they might do if it has a better Edition) that Joker will be able to appear as a duplicate again even if the Showman is sold.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Red Deck gives +1 Discard which makes it easier to find a 6.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Blue Deck gives +1 Hand which allows the player more freedom to utilize Sixth Sense, as there are more remaining Hands to defeat the Blind.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck increase the chance to draw a 6 as they have less overall cards.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Painted Deck gives +2 hand size, making it easier to find 6s. However, the -1 joker slot makes Sixth Sense riskier to use.

name: Sixth Sense
text: High Card is the only poker hand directly relevant to Sixth Sense.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Perkeo can copy any Spectral card created by Sixth Sense.

name: Sixth Sense
text: DNA can create copies of playing cards, allowing the player to infinitely farm Spectral cards as long as the Deck contains at least one 6. The order of the two makes no difference—If DNA is on the right, the 6 will still be replicated after being destroyed.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Erosion will also scale after Sixth Sense destroys 6s.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Drunkard and Merry Andy both give extra discards, which makes it easier to find a 6. While Merry Andy reduces hand size, which normally makes 6s harder to find, the extra discards will make that punishment pretty much meaningless, as long as the player does not reduce their hand size much lower.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Juggler increases hand size and makes it easier to find a 6 to play. Troubadour and Turtle Bean can be used too, but Troubadour removes a hand, which makes it more punishing to use Sixth Sense, and Turtle Bean

name: Sixth Sense
text: Black Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Golden Needle Deck all reduce the number of hands to play, which can discourage using Sixth Sense while a player's hands aren't strong enough.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Nebula Deck only starts with one Consumable Slot, which makes it harder to hold onto Sixth Sense's Spectral cards.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Obtaining a second copy of Sixth Sense does not stack with itself, creating only 1 Spectral card when destroying 6s.

name: Sixth Sense
text: While Burglar gives more hands to play with, it also removes all discards. If the first hand of the round does not contain a 6, Sixth Sense will miss its effect.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Stuntman reduces hand size, which makes it harder to find a 6.

name: Sixth Sense
text: The Psychic forces the player to play a 5-card hand, meaning Sixth Sense cannot activate.

name: Sixth Sense
text: The Needle sets the player's hands to 1. Therefore, to still benefit fr

name: Sixth Sense
text: As Sixth Sense requires having 6s in the deck to activate, it has limited use as the player will likely destroy all 6s in the Deck before reaching Ante 8. However, this is usually ideal, as 6s do not have any particularly strong synergies with other Jokers, and the Spectral card given may help further enhance the player's deck and hasten the Deck manipulation process. In general, Spectral cards to look out for are:

name: Sixth Sense
text: Any of the Seal-adding cards.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Deja Vu, Trance, Medium, and Talisman.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Aura for farming the Polychrome Edition.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Cryptid to make copies of a useful card, which can be used in conjunction with the above Spectral cards.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Immolate to further hasten Deck manipulation and for a boost in Money.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Ectoplasm for when the player has their final Joker lineup.

name: Sixth Sense
text: Any other Spectral card is still worth keeping so as to prevent it from appearing in the shop, either from a Spectral Pack or from playing on the Ghost Deck, as they are either too niche or hard to make use of.

name: Sixth Sense
text: When using Sixth Sense, it can be worth opening Standard Packs to directly add 6s for later destruction; while this usually isn't as good as opening a Spectral Pack directly, Standard Packs are much more common than Spectral Packs, and Spectral cards can be quite impactful. Additionally, Sixth Sense makes it more reasonable to fish for specific or highly-upgraded car

name: Sly Joker
text: The Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck, having fewer total cards in the deck, gives a higher chance of drawing a pair.

name: Sly Joker
text: The Erratic Deck will have cards of a certain rank appear more than others.

name: Sly Joker
text: Plasma Deck benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand.

name: Sly Joker
text: Sly Joker triggers whenever there are two duplicate scoring cards, regardless of whether the hand itself is a "Pair". This means you can trigger Sly Joker if you play a Flush that contains two of the same card.

name: Sly Joker
text: In an unmodified deck, Sly Joker triggers off of every hand in the game except for High Card, Flush, Straight, or Straight Flush.

name: Sly Joker
text: Jolly Joker and The Duo pair well with this, as both will trigger on the same activation as this joker.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Black Deck: The +1 Joker Slot allows Smeared Joker to function as a utility Joker while still providing space for 5 other Jokers to score.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Checkered Deck is split between two suits that do not combine due to the Smeared Joker, so it loses out on some benefits. However, it allows the deck to benefit from effects that involve Clubs and Diamonds, including very powerful Jokers like Ancient Joker, so it can still be quite valuable.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Painted Deck's hand size of 10 guarantees a Flush with Smeared Joker and no Stones. However, with Painted Deck's fewer Joker slots, keeping effect Jokers like Smeared Joker can be risky.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Works best with the following hands if you are trying to go for a flush build.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Flush

name: Smeared Joker
text: Straight Flush

name: Smeared Joker
text: Flush House

name: Smeared Joker
text: Flush Five

name: Smeared Joker
text: Generally, any Joker that takes effect upon cards of certain suits will benefit from Smeared Joker, by activating on more cards, including:

name: Smeared Joker
text: Lusty Joker and Greedy Joker - Each Diamonds or Hearts provides +3 Mult.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Wrathful Joker and Gluttonous Joker - Each Clubs or Spades provides +3 Mult.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Bloodstone - Each Diamonds or Hearts has a 1 in 2 chance to provide a X1.5 Mult.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Rough Gem - Each Diamonds or Hearts

name: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker doubles a player's vulnerability to suit bosses:

name: Smeared Joker
text: The Head and The Window both debuff all Diamonds and Hearts cards.

name: Smeared Joker
text: The Club and The Goad both debuff all Clubs and Spades cards.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Despite Smeared Joker counting suits as other suits, Jokers that unlock based on a certain suit won't count the other suit for their unlock condition, which includes the following Jokers:

name: Smeared Joker
text: Rough Gem won't count Hearts cards for its unlock condition.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Bloodstone won't count Diamonds cards for its unlock condition.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Arrowhead won't count Clubs cards for its unlock condition.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Onyx Agate won't count Spades cards for its unlock condition.

name: Smeared Joker
text: Shoot the Moon does not need to play Diamonds cards in order to get unlocked.

name: Smeared Joker
text: There is one exception, however, which is Seeing Double, which can be unlocked by playing 7s of Spades with Smeared Joker.

name: Smiley Face
text: Red Deck's extra discard can be used to dig for more face cards in the player's deck.

name: Smiley Face
text: Painted Deck has a larger hand size, allowing for more face cards to appear. However, the -1 Joker slot means Smiley Face may not be as viable as some other options.

name: Smiley Face
text: Mad World Deck starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which makes every card scored provide +5 Mult.

name: Smiley Face
text: Two Pair and especially Full House work best with this Joker in the early game.

name: Smiley Face
text: Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind, and Flush Five work well with this Joker in the late game.

name: Smiley Face
text: Pareidolia makes every card scored provide +5 Mult, effectively making every card a slightly better Mult.

name: Smiley Face
text: Sock and Buskin will add an additional +5 Mult per face card scored.

name: Smiley Face
text: Triboulet provides a Mult multiplier for each played King or Queen.

name: Smiley Face
text: Business Card gives each face card played a 50% chance to provide $2 when scored.

name: Smiley Face
text: Scary Face provides additional Chips for each face card played.

name: Smiley Face
text: Splash causes all face cards played to provide +5 Mult.

name: Smiley Face
text: Baron, Shoot the Moon, and Reserved Parking encourage not playing face cards.

name: Smiley Face
text: Ride the Bus actively punishes playing face cards.

name: Smiley Face
text: Canio's ability activates only upon destroying face cards, resulting in fewer cards able to trigger Smiley Face.

name: Smiley Face
text: The Plant debuffs all faces, which prevents Smiley Face from giving any mult.

name: Sock and Buskin
text: Mad World Deck works well with Sock and Buskin, as this deck starts with Pareidolia and Business Card, allowing all cards to retrigger and generate more money from Business Card.

name: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers' usefulness is comparable to a bell curve over time. Initially, Spare Trousers has no bonus, and the player needs to play a Two Pair hand for it to have any benefit at all. Since any played hand can only ever include one Two Pair at a time, it can potentially take numerous hands and rounds of a run to build up Spare Trousers to a point where it feels strong. In other words, Spare Trousers requires a significant time investment, plus a conscious effort to play as many Two Pair hands as possible. Furthermore, since it can only be increased by +2 Mult per hand at most, in the late game (beginning around Ante level 7 and higher) the player runs the risk of being unable to increase Spare Trousers quickly enough to keep it viable. Usually, the player can raise Spare Trousers to around +40 Mult by the time they reach Ante level 8, but if Spare Trousers was the centerpiece of their build, they may struggle against the Showdown Blind and any subsequent Boss Blinds. Using Planet cards to level up Spare Trousers' applicable hands can partially compensate for the joker's late-game strength falloff.

name: Steel Joker
text: To synergize with the Steel Joker, there are two approaches: one is to maximize the number of Steel cards in the deck, and the second is to maximize the scoring potential of the Steel cards that will be in your hand. In general, Steel cards benefit from having a high base multiplier after scoring the cards, since Steel cards act before any Jokers. As such, Planet cards and Jokers that add multiplier upon scoring cards can help boost scores.

name: Steel Joker

Since the combination of multipliers between Steel Joker and Steel cards can significantly boost mult well beyond any possible chip combinations, Plasma helps turn that high mult into a much higher score.

name: Supernova
text: Supernova works well with all decks, though it can find particular synergy when playing with a strategy that matches the deck to the poker hand, like Checkered Deck and Flush.

name: Supernova
text: The key to Supernova is to play the same hand consistently. Hands that can reliably be made, especially in the early game, help Supernova flourish. Furthermore, the more hands played, the better, so a build focusing on high base mult and chips hands (like straight flush) can prevent you from using all your hands to boost Supernova. This makes Supernova particularly powerful when matched with hands like High Card or Pair.

text: Shortcut: Normally, there are only two possible straights that contain an ace: A/2/3/4/5 and 10/J/Q/K/A. This makes it relatively difficult to trigger Superposition. Shortcut, however, allows straights to skip single cards, vastly increasing the number of ways this joker can be triggered.

name: Superposition
text: Mathematically, assuming a standard 52-card deck: the number of 5-card hands that trigger Superposition increases by a factor of 12 with the addition of Four Fingers, a factor of 16 with the addition of Shortcut, and a factor of 84 with both. Meanwhile, the chance of getting any straight at all increases by a factor of 12.2 with the addition of Four Fingers, a factor of 12.8 with the addition of Shortcut, and a factor of 76.3 with both.

text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck work well with this Joker thanks to their smaller deck, making searching for Four of a Kind easier.

name: The Family
text: Erratic Deck can work well with this Joker if it randomizes a lot of cards with the same rank.

name: The Family
text: The Family will trigger on any hand containing a Four of a Kind:

name: The Family
text: Four of a Kind

name: The Family
text: Five of a Kind

name: The Family
text: Flush Five

name: The Family
text: Any jokers that trigger with Three of a Kind hands and Pair hands, such as Zany Joker and The Duo.

name: The Family
text: Drunkard and Merry Andy give extra discards, which makes it easier to find a Four of a Kind. Merry Andy's hand size downside is pretty much meaningless with the extra discards, as long as the player does not reduce their hand size much further.

name: The Family
text: Juggler and Troubadour increase hand size, which makes it easier to find a Four of a Kind. Troubadour's -1 hand punishment is pretty much meaningless on early antes as a single X4 Mult can beat some antes with good + Mult. Turtle Bean can also be used, but not permanently like the other 2 Jokers.

name: The Idol
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck can make it easier to manipulate the deck into one type of card due to the reduced number of starting cards.

name: The Idol
text: Zodiac Deck starts with Tarot Merchant, which can be helpful to manipulate the deck in your favor using Tarot cards.

name: The Idol
text: Checkered Deck starts with 2 of every card rather than 1, making The Idol slightly more consistent to activate in the early game.

name: The Idol
text: Flush Five works exceptionally well with The Idol because it can trigger the effect 5 times, plus any additional retriggers from Jokers or Red Seal.

name: The Idol
text: If using The Idol, it's best to play a Flush Five as soon as possible in order to unlock its respective Planet card, Eris.

name: The Idol
text: In the early to midgame, one can make do with Three of a Kind and Four of a Kind, assuming the correct card is chosen by The Idol. Due to the highly random nature of the card, you will likely want more reliable sources of score before you can fully utilize it. That said, using this Joker in the early to midgame is nearly impossible.

name: The Idol
text: Jokers that retrigger scored cards, such as Dusk or Hack, will compound the multiplication immensely.

name: The Idol
text: Jokers that help manipulate the deck to fewer types of cards will make the randomly chosen card more likely to be desirable. DNA or Trading Card are the most important jokers for accomplishing this.

name: The Idol
text: Smeared Joker effectively halves

name: The Idol
text: Hologram requires you to add cards to your deck for Joker scaling, making this Joker more inconsistent in scoring, unless you add your desired cards with DNA.

name: The Idol
text: Certificate always adds cards with a random rank and suit, making an awkward combo with The Idol.

name: The Idol
text: The rank and suit are decided by pulling a random non-Stone from your deck. Thus, if you have multiples of a particular rank or suit, it will be proportionally likely for that value to be chosen.

name: The Idol
text: While it can be underwhelming early game, it excels late game when the proper deck manipulation can be put into place. A Flush Five containing five of The Idol's target card yields X32 Mult, retriggers notwithstanding. However, it is one of the more difficult Jokers to extract the most use out of.

name: The Idol
text: The best cards to build around are those that can be retriggered more times by other Jokers. 2's, 3's, 4's, and 5's can be retriggered by Hack, while face cards (J, Q, K) can be retriggered by Sock and Buskin.

name: The Order
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck both have fewer cards than usual, which makes it easier to make Straights.

name: The Order
text: Painted Deck's extra hand size makes Straights easier to find.

name: The Order
text: 15 Minute City Deck starts with an Eternal Shortcut, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand.

name: The Order
text: The Order will trigger on Straights and Straight Flushes.

name: The Order
text: As all Straight hands have high Chip scaling from Planet cards, The Order can lend itself well to high-level Straight or Straight Flush runs.

name: The Order
text: Four Fingers and Shortcut both allow Straights to be made more easily. Having either of these will make Straight builds much more reliable, making The Order easier to trigger.

name: The Order
text: Jokers that give bonuses when Straights are played, like Crazy Joker and Devious Joker, work well with The Order. Runner is the primary example of this, as it gives scaling Chips when the player plays the hand they already want to play if they have The Order.

name: The Order
text: Sources of easy +Mult are useful in the early antes, such as Mystic Summit, as they allow The Order to multiply a larger amount of Mult without having to level Straights first.

name: The Order
text: Erratic Deck can make it difficult to use The Order, as the randomized rank and suit makes it harder to form Straights.

name: The Order
text: Five-Card Draw Deck's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights.

name: The Order
text: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, have anti-synergy with The Order, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights.

name: The Order
text: Ectoplasm and Ouija have anti-synergy with The Order, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but Ouija converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights less consistent.

name: The Order
text: The Manacle's -1 hand size makes it hard to assemble Straights.

name: The Order
text: The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very ha

name: The Tribe
text: Checkered Deck will almost always get value from The Tribe, since it excels at making Flushes.

name: The Tribe
text: Flush: The hand this Joker is specifically made for.

name: The Tribe
text: Straight Flush: A much more valuable hand, use Tarot cards and Standard Packs to make playing a Straight Flush easier.

name: The Tribe
text: Flush House/Flush Five: The two most valuable base hands in the game, which both contain Flushes. Try to pick up cards that make playing these possible.

name: The Tribe
text: Four Fingers and Smeared Joker make it easier to play Flushes and trigger this Joker's multiplier.

name: The Tribe
text: Any Joker that adds multiplier based on played cards of certain suit, such as Gluttonous Joker.

name: The Tribe
text: Troubadour gives extra hand size, making it easier to find cards of the same suit.

name: The Tribe
text: Crafty Joker and Droll Joker trigger on the same condition, giving them natural synergy.

name: The Tribe
text: Tarot cards:

name: The Tribe
text: The Moon, The Star, The Sun, and The World turn cards into Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, and Spades, respectively, which can be useful if the player wants their deck to focus on one or two suits.

name: The Tribe
text: The Hanged Man can be useful for cutting unwanted cards out the deck if the player wants to focus on one particular card suit.

name: The Tribe
text: The Lovers turn a card into a Wild, which can be useful for forming a Flush if the player is down a card or two needed.

name: The Tribe
text: The Flush does not need to score for The Tribe to activate. This can happen when playing a Four of a Kind with 5 cards of the same suit (ex: K K K K 8 of Spades).

name: The Trio
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck work well with this Joker thanks to their smaller deck, allowing assembling a Three of a Kind easier.

name: The Trio
text: Erratic Deck can work well with this Joker if it randomizes a lot of cards with the same rank.

name: The Trio
text: This Joker can trigger on any played hand containing three cards of the same rank:

name: The Trio
text: Three of a Kind, Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind

name: The Trio
text: Full House, Flush House

name: The Trio
text: Flush Five

name: The Trio
text: Flush, when a Three of a Kind is present in the played hand

name: The Trio
text: Wily Joker gives +100 Chips when played hand contains a Three of a Kind.

name: The Trio
text: Zany Joker gives +12 Mult when played hand contains a Three of a Kind.

name: The Trio
text: Playing a Three of a Kind or above will also trigger Jokers that trigger with Pair hands such as Jolly Joker and The Duo.

name: The Trio
text: The Three of a Kind does not need to score for The Trio to activate. The only way to have this happen is when playing a Flush with Four Fingers that also has a differently suited Three of a Kind (ex: ♠️10 ♠️10 ♦️10 ♠️4 ♠️3).

name: Throwback
text: Anaglyph Deck can be useful when running Throwback, as the Double Tags it generates make skipping Blinds more appealing.

name: Throwback
text: Fragile Deck can work with Throwback, as this deck encourages the player to preserve as many Glasss as possible to beat ante 8, for which skipping blinds can be useful.

name: Throwback
text: Jokers that have powerful up-front effects generally work great with Throwback, as they allow you to skip blinds and boost Throwback without compromising the other Jokers' scaling. Flat +Mult jokers in particular, such as Half Joker, Mystic Summit, etc., can provide a larger base mult for Throwback, though depending on the hand type, per-card mult boosts may be stronger.

name: Throwback
text: Since Throwback can boost mult to very high values, it can be worth investing in a +Chips joker, like Stuntman or Bull, to improve that side of the equation.

name: Throwback
text: Since Throwback prioritizes skipping blinds, consumable Jokers (Popcorn, Ice Cream, Seltzer, and similar) go through fewer hands, allowing them to be useful for more Antes.

name: Throwback
text: Diet Cola empowers the skips you do, allowing you to double the bonus from a strong tag.

name: Throwback
text: Glasss work very well with Throwback, as you can gain X2 Mult, and the risk of losing the cards is reduced because you are playing fewer hands.

name: Throwback
text: Hieroglyph and Petroglyph lower the Ante by 1, giving another

name: Throwback
text: Because Throwback needs to skip Blinds to scale, it is usually a poor combination with Jokers that require action taken in Blinds or the shop to scale. For example, Hologram, Vampire, Supernova, and Madness. It can be decent if a couple of blinds were skipped in the past as a temporary midgame choice, but there are often better alternatives for builds that use these kinds of scaling.

name: To Do List
text: Red Deck gives +1 Discard, allowing the player more chances to dig through their deck if To Do List requires a more difficult hand to play.

name: To Do List
text: Blue Deck gives +1 Hand, meaning that the player has more chances to get more Money from To Do List.

name: To Do List
text: Ghost Deck and Zodiac Deck have increased access to Spectral cards and Tarot cards respectively, which can make some of the more difficult hands easier to achieve if To Do List chooses them.

name: To Do List
text: Erratic Deck can make hands like Four of a Kind easier to play. However, it can also make it harder to play hands like Straight.

name: To Do List
text: The target hand will change randomly every round, so it doesn't synergise with any specific hand.

name: To Do List
text: Burglar adds 3 extra hands allowing To Do list to generate more money.

name: To Do List
text: Drunkard and Merry Andy add more discards which can help the player to find the hand that To Do List chose.

name: To Do List
text: Blueprint and Brainstorm can copy To Do List to effectively double/triple amount of money gained with no downside as they can be moved around to buff scoring Jokers afterward.

name: To Do List
text: Four Fingers, Shortcut and Smeared Joker all make certain hands easier to play.

name: To Do List
text: Grabber and Nacho Tong both give extra hands allowing To Do List to generate more money.

name: To Do List
text: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give extra discards allowing the player to find the hand that To Do List chose.

name: To Do List
text: Black Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Golden Needle Deck don't allow the player many chances for To Do List to trigger due to their reduced number of hands.

name: To Do List
text: Any joker which incentivizes playing a consistent hand type throughout a run like Runner, Supernova or Spare Trousers has a slight anti-synergy with To Do list.

name: To Do List
text: When running Obelisk, it is possible for To Do List to land on your most played hand.

name: To Do List
text: To Do List only applies to the scoring hand, not the hands that it contains. For example, playing a Full House if the chosen hand is Two Pair does not give $4.

name: To Do List
text: Each copy of To Do List picks its Poker Hand independently of every other copy. For example, if one were to copy a held To Do List that is on Straight Flush using Ankh, they will both start at Straight Flush. However, once they reset, it is possible that one is on Full House and the other is on High Card. This is unlike all other Jokers with similar random effects (such as Mail-In Rebate, Castle, or Ancient Joker), as all of their copies are "synced".

name: To Do List
text: Much like the appearance of planet cards, it has a chance to choose Secret hands if they have been played at least once during the current run.

name: To the Moon
text: Yellow Deck, as this deck tends to allow the player to reach the initial Interest cap earlier.

name: To the Moon
text: Jokers that rely on Money, like Bull and Red Card, are boosted from the extra Interest To the Moon offers.

name: To the Moon
text: Money generating jokers that provide Money during the round, like Rough Gem and Mail-In Rebate can help the player reach Interest thresholds.

name: To the Moon
text: Golds and Gold Seal allow money generation mid-round, meaning the money they make counts toward interest earned at the end.

name: To the Moon
text: Seed Money and Money Tree have one of the strongest synergies with To The Moon, as they raise the base interest cap. With both vouchers, To the Moon can end up producing $40 at the end of every round.

name: To the Moon
text: Avoid this Joker on Green Deck and Mad World Deck, as those decks cannot gain interest at any time.

name: To the Moon
text: Luxury Tax Deck receives little benefit from To The Moon, as in order to take advantage of its high interest, the player would want high starting money, which this deck punishes.

name: To the Moon
text: Vagabond encourages playing without earning interest, making To The Moon useless.

name: To the Moon
text: Credit Card enables going $20 in debt, well below the minimum interest level.

name: To the Moon
text: The Ox sets money to $0 when playing most played hand, which totably disables To the Moon (unless the player has Matador)

name: To the Moon
text: The Tooth deducts money for every card played, so try not to play any 5-card hand if possible.

name: To the Moon
text: The Omelette Deck challenge bans To the Moon.

name: Trading Card
text: Red Deck gives +1 Discard, allowing Trading Card to be used with fewer consequences.

name: Trading Card
text: In the early game, Trading Card tends to work best with hands that are more likely to be drawn, since it requires "wasting" a discard.

name: Trading Card
text: However, Trading Card is one of the strongest enablers for more difficult hands by the mid/late game, as removing a third to a half of the deck makes certain difficult hand types significantly easier to assemble.

name: Trading Card
text: Drunkard gives +1 Discard, allowing Trading Card to be used with fewer consequences.

name: Trading Card
text: Merry Andy gives +3 Discards, making the discard used for Trading Card inconsequential.

name: Trading Card
text: Glass Joker increases by X0.75 Mult for every destroyed Glass card.

name: Trading Card
text: Canio increases by X1 Mult for every destroyed face card, dramatically improving the value of Trading Card.

name: Trading Card
text: Erosion gives +4 Mult for every card less than the deck's starting amount.

name: Trading Card
text: Ride the Bus is easier to keep the effect of, as face cards can be destroyed.

name: Trading Card
text: DNA pairs well with Trading Card for deck manipulation.

name: Trading Card
text: Hologram scales on adding cards. By using Trading Card, cards can be added without bloating the deck.

name: Trading Card
text: Mystic Summit gains +15 Mult after using up all discards, making the discard used for Trading Card less consequential.

name: Trading Card
text: Purple Seal activates before the destruction, resulting in both a Tarot card and $3.

name: Trading Card
text: Wasteful and

name: Trading Card
text: Blast Off Deck starts with 2 discards, making Trading Card harder to use.

name: Trading Card
text: Fragile Deck makes it risky to use Trading Card without Glass Joker.

name: Trading Card
text: Jokers that discourage discarding do not benefit from the required discard to activate Trading Card.

name: Trading Card
text: These include Green Joker, Ramen, Banner, and Delayed Gratification.

name: Trading Card
text: Burglar removes all discards, rendering Trading Card unusable.

name: Trading Card
text: May or may not have anti-synergy with Burnt Joker since Trading Card requires discarding a single card to activate meaning Burnt Joker can only level-up High Card.

name: Trading Card
text: The Water starts with 0 discards, meaning Trading Card cannot be used.

name: Trading Card
text: Blue Stake starts with -1 discard, making Trading Card harder to use.

name: Trading Card
text: If the player holds multiple copies of Trading Card, they still only apply to the first discard, and each gives $3. Trading Card cannot be copied by Blueprint or Brainstorm, but multiple copies can be obtained via Showman, Invisible Joker, or Ankh.

name: Triboulet
text: Most decks benefit equally from Triboulet as most start with the same amount of Kings and Queen.

name: Triboulet
text: The Ghost Deck has easier access to Spectral cards, which simplifies deck building, allowing the deck to be more concentrated on Kings and Queens, but also because of Red Seals, which can retrigger Triboulet's effect.

name: Triboulet
text: To make the most value out of Triboulet, bigger poker hands are preferred, such as Full House, Flush House, Five of a Kind or Flush Five. This also means that, inversely, smaller poker hands like High Card or Pair get less triggers of Triboulet, and therefore are not recommended.

name: Triboulet
text: As Kings and Queens are considered face cards, any Jokers triggering off of face cards naturally make a combo with Triboulet. Retriggers are by far the most valuable, as seen with Sock and Buskin, activating the multiplicative Mult up to 5 times more. This skyrockets gain from Triboulet when playing a 5-card hand containing only scoring Kings and Queens which is X32 Mult to X1024 Mult, a staggering difference.

name: Triboulet
text: Hanging Chad, Dusk, and Seltzer are also good due to the same reasoning.

name: Triboulet
text: Splash allows Kings and Queens to score on poker hands they otherwise would be unable to, such as an Ace-high High Card hand.

name: Triboulet
text: Tarot cards:

name: Triboulet
text: The Empress can enhance Queens or Kings into Mults, which prov

name: Triboulet
text: Abandoned Deck, Medusa Deck, and Mad World Deck are not recommended due to the lack of initial Kings and Queens.

name: Triboulet
text: Canio requires many face cards to be destroyed, the majority of which tend to be Kings and Queens. This isn't too much of a problem if the player decides to destroy just Jacks or if they have Pareidolia.

name: Triboulet
text: Baron, Shoot the Moon and Reserved Parking require having Kings and Queens held in hand instead of playing them, making a bad combination with Triboulet.

name: Triboulet
text: Though Reserved Parking isn't too much of an issue if the player leaves just Jacks or have Pareidolia.

name: Triboulet
text: Ride the Bus grows with every consecutive hand played that contains no face cards, meaning consistently playing Kings or Queens renders it useless.

name: Triboulet
text: The Plant can be a run killer as debuffed Queens

name: Troubadour
text: Blue Deck works best with Troubadour thanks to its +1 hand per round bonus, offsetting the -1 hand penalty of this Joker. This effectively transforms the Blue Deck into a more flexible Painted Deck.

name: Troubadour
text: Golden Needle Deck starts with 1 hand, and Troubadour cannot reduce hands below one, turning Troubadour into a +2 hand size without any penalty.

name: Troubadour
text: Any strong 5 card hands can benefit from Troubadour, as the increased hand size means a higher chance to draw needed cards to form the hand.

name: Troubadour
text: Troubadour can also be good in High-card builds that rely on cards being in hand to score, such as with Baron or Steel cards.

name: Troubadour
text: Any held-in-hand effect Joker will be improved by Troubadour by virtue of holding more cards in hand.

name: Troubadour
text: This includes Baron, as mentioned previously, Shoot the Moon, and Reserved Parking.

name: Troubadour
text: Mime: More cards in hand means more cards for Mime to retrigger.

name: Troubadour
text: Mail-In Rebate: With increased hand size, it can be easier to find the card rank required for that round.

name: Troubadour
text: Burglar: Add three extra hands, offsetting the -1 hand penalty of this Joker at the cost of no discards.

name: Troubadour
text: Merry Andy and Stuntman: Troubadour offsets the hand size penalty of these two Jokers.

name: Troubadour
text: With Troubadour's increased hand size, it can make it easier to draw into Steels and/or Golds, as well as cards that have a Blue Seal.

name: Troubadour
text: Black Deck makes it difficult to use Troubadour on, as its -1 hand per round penalty means players will only have 2 hands to beat each blind.

name: Troubadour
text: Similarly, Blast Off Deck makes it even more difficult to use Troubadour on, as its -1 hand per round penalty means players will only have 1 hand to beat each blind.

name: Troubadour
text: Overall, any scaling Joker that requires hands to be played is impeded by the -1 hand penalty, giving fewer opportunities to scale them efficiently.

name: Troubadour
text: This includes Green Joker, Ride the Bus, Supernova, Runner, Square Joker, Spare Trousers, and Obelisk.

name: Troubadour
text: Vagabond and Space Joker suffer from the -1 hand penalty, as Jokers that generate a resource or trigger when a hand is played have fewer opportunities to trigger.

name: Troubadour
text: Card Sharp can activate one less time.

name: Troubadour
text: Loyalty Card becomes harder

name: Troubadour
text: The Five-Card Draw Deck challenge bans Troubadour.

name: Troubadour
text: Because the hand is taken away when Blind is selected, gaining Troubadour during a round will not reduce the amount of hands until the next Blind, and selling Troubadour during a blind will only remove the extra Hand Size while keeping the -1 hand effect for that Blind.

name: Troubadour
text: Troubadour can never decrease the total amount of hands below 1, even with multiple copies or when used during The Needle or Golden Needle Deck.

name: Turtle Bean
text: Any deck can benefit from Turtle Bean.

name: Turtle Bean
text: Any 5-card hand can benefit from Turtle Bean. In particular, the extra hand size makes finding matching cards for high-value hands, like Straight Flush or Flush Five, much easier.

name: Turtle Bean
text: If your goal is huge hand sizes, then:

name: Turtle Bean
text: Juggler: +1 hand size.

name: Turtle Bean
text: Troubadour: +2 hand size, at the cost of -1 hand per round.

name: Turtle Bean
text: Turtle Bean has particular synergies with:

name: Turtle Bean
text: Any Joker that provides held in-hand bonuses like Baron, Shoot the Moon, or Reserved Parking benefits, since Turtle Bean allows larger hand sizes.

name: Turtle Bean
text: Throwback: Since Throwback benefits from skipping blinds, this extends the life of Turtle Bean.

name: Turtle Bean
text: Note that the increased Hand Size from Turtle Bean also applies to Tarot and Spectral packs. Thus:

name: Turtle Bean
text: Tarot and Spectral cards with selected card effects have a wider selection of cards to choose from your deck.

name: Turtle Bean
text: Ouija and Sigil convert substantially more cards if used early in Turtle Bean's duration.

name: Turtle Bean
text: Because Turtle Bean lasts exactly 5 rounds, the Perishable sticker has no effect on it, as it will get disappear immediately before it is set to be debuffed.

name: Turtle Bean
text: If Crimson Heart disables Turtle Bean, the hand size will return to normal, but current cards in hand will stay intact until

name: Turtle Bean
text: Blackboard can be harder to trigger, as the increased hand size can make it harder to hold only Clubs and Spades in your hand.

name: Turtle Bean
text: The increased hand size will make it hard for Raised Fist to give more score from high-ranked cards.

name: Turtle Bean
text: The sell value of Turtle Bean does not depend on its current Hand Size value, so it is best to sell Turtle Bean when it is at +1 Hand Size, instead of letting it get destroyed (worth $0).

name: Vagabond
text: Green Deck isn't reliant on Interest to gain money, so spending everything you have to trigger Vagabond won't impact your ability to buy from the Shop as much.

name: Vagabond
text: However, some of Green Deck's income is from leftover Hands/Discards, which can be harder to save if the player wants to get max value from Vagabond by playing all their hands.

name: Vagabond
text: Blue Deck allows more hands to be played, meaning more triggers of Vagabond.

name: Vagabond
text: Magic Deck's extra consumable slot is very helpful for saving useful Tarots.

name: Vagabond
text: Zodiac Deck's unique shop makes it easier to spend money to reach the $4 threshold and generally helps the Tarot-stacking builds Vagabond tends to form.

name: Vagabond
text: Luxury Tax Deck encourages the player to not have too much money when entering blinds, similar to Vagabond.

name: Vagabond
text: Weaker hands like High Card or Pair allow the player to farm more Tarot cards per round.

name: Vagabond
text: Later in the game, these Tarot cards can enable hands built around one rank, such as Four of a Kind and Five of a Kind.

name: Vagabond
text: Jokers that scale based on hands played, like Ride the Bus, Square Joker, and Obelisk, are helpful to pair with Vagabond, as they grow more powerful in the process of using Vagabond to its full potential.

name: Vagabond
text: Furthering this idea, Burglar allows more hands to be played to both generate more Tarots and scale these Jokers.

name: Vagabond
text: Jokers that want the player to use many Tarot cards benefit well from Vagab

name: Vagabond
text: Black Deck, Blast Off Deck, and Golden Needle Deck don't work as well with Vagabond due to their reduced number of hands.

name: Vagabond
text: Nebula Deck's fewer consumable slots make it significantly harder to use the Tarots from Vagabond.

name: Vagabond
text: Rich get Richer Deck doesn't work well with Vagabond, as this deck encourages the player to have a lot of money.

name: Vagabond
text: Jokers which generate money during a round, as opposed to at cashout, can quickly pass Vagabond's shutoff point.

name: Vagabond
text: Rough Gem, To Do List, Mail-In Rebate, Business Card, Reserved Parking and Matador all can pass Vagabond's requirement during the round.

name: Vagabond
text: Trading Card's $3 does not go over the limit on its own, but it does require the player make sure they have no more than one dollar before each Blind.

name: Vampire
text: Zodiac Deck, Magic Deck or the Ghost Deck work well for the vampire, as these decks have more opportunities to obtain Tarots and Spectral cards (see Consumables below) that can provide enhanced cards to feed the Vampire.

name: Vampire
text: Black Deck's additional Joker slot can be used for effect Jokers (like Midas Mask) to generate enhanced cards.

name: Vampire
text: Medusa Deck and Monolith Deck Challenge Decks both starts with a Marble Joker, which Vampire can use it as an enhancement generator to scale easier. Not only that, Medusa also starts with 12 Stones.

name: Vampire
text: Since this joker will consume the Enhancements before they get applied, hands with a high base mult are preferred.

name: Vampire
text: Flush Five

name: Vampire
text: Flush House

name: Vampire
text: Five of a Kind

name: Vampire
text: Straight Flush

name: Vampire
text: Full House

name: Vampire
text: Flush

name: Vampire
text: Four of a Kind

name: Vampire
text: Vampire combos well with jokers that either generate Tarot cards, or enhancements themselves (such as Midas Mask) to generate a steady supply of Enhancements to eat.

name: Vampire
text: If using the Midas Mask combo, the order will affect this. If the Midas Mask is placed first, face cards will be changed to Golds, and the Vampire will immediately consume the effect to increase its multiplier. However, if the Midas Mask is placed after the Vampire, the cards are made golden without consuming the effect. Thus, players could create infinite enhancement supplies for Va

name: Vampire
text: Jokers that rely on specific card enhancements become harder to use when combined with Vampire. These include Lucky Cat, Glass Joker, Golden Ticket, Steel Joker and Stone Joker.

name: Vampire
text: Driver's License limits the players to not play any enhanced card, making a risky combo with Vampire.

name: Vampire
text: Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon reduce the probabilities of Tarot cards appearing in the shop, and therefore, the X Mult from Vampire. Magic Trick also applies here, but this one isn't too bad at all since it's required to get Illusion.

name: Vampire
text: Vampire removes Enhancements before their effect occurs, meaning the Enhancements cannot activate. All scored cards will get their Enhancements removed. Vampire also cannot change the type of Poker Hand retroactively, for example removing Wild would still keep the Poker Hand as Flush.

name: Vampire
text: There are a few notable playing card interactions:

name: Vampire
text: Debuffed: Debuffed cards are considered not to have any Modifier including Enhancements, so Vampire cannot remove Enhancements from debuffed cards.

name: Vampire
text: Wild: wild enhancement gets removed, the card scores if it would have scored for the original hand, and the type of hand played is not affected.

name: Vampire
text: Glass: glass enhancement gets removed, no X2 Mult, and there is no chance for the card to break.

name: Vampire
text: Stone: stone enhancement gets removed and card returns to what it originally was, no +50 Chips, but card will always score for this hand (the type of hand played is not affected).

name: Vampire
text: Editions: Editions are not Enhancements, will not get removed by Vampire, and work normally.

name: Vampire
text: Seals: Seals are not Enhancements, will not get removed by Vampire, and work normally.

name: Vampire
text: The Joker order matters significantly when using certain other Jokers with Vampire:

name: Vampire
text: A second Vampire: only the left-most Vampire can remove enhancements and scale at any time (regardless of how many Midas Masks are used).

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Any Deck synergizes well with Walkie Talkie due to its versatility. However, these have a slightly easier time using it than the others:

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Abandoned Deck: Has the highest state of advantage with this Joker, due to having less cards in the Deck overall, thereby making it easier to find 10s and 4s.

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Painted Deck: This Joker serves as good role compression, providing Chips and Additive Mult while taking up just 1 of the 4 Joker slots. On top of this, the increased hand size allows easier finding of higher quantities of 10s and 4s.

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Ghost Deck, Magic Deck, and Zodiac Deck: All these have more overall access to the Deck fixing methods that this Joker loves, but they do not have a distinct consistency advantage right away like the aforementioned ones do.

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Focus on these hands in the early game to consistently maximize this Joker's impact:

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Two Pair

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Three of a Kind

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Full House (the best choice, due to having 5 scoring cards while not being substantially harder to find)

name: Walkie Talkie
text: As you manipulate your Deck to include more 10s and 4s, pivot towards these hands (note that 3 of these 4 are secret hands, meaning you will not be able to level scale them right away):

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Four of a Kind

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Five of a Kind

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Flush House

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Flush Five

name: Walkie Talkie
text: Mad World Deck doesn't start with any 10s, which makes Walkie Talkie weaker.

name: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker synergizes well with all Decks fairly equally, but some have minor advantages over the others.

name: Wee Joker
text: Most decks have the same starting amount of four 2s, making Wee Joker synergize with them fairly equally. However, some decks have features that may make utilizing Wee Joker easier:

name: Wee Joker
text: Red Deck: The extra Discard allows the player to cycle through more cards, which helps with finding and scoring 2s greatly.

name: Wee Joker
text: Blue Deck: The extra Hand lets the player use a "throwaway" hand for extra scaling, and also acts as a pseudo-Discard, again helping with finding and scoring 2s.

name: Wee Joker
text: Magic Deck: With the help of the two starting copies of The Fool, the player can potentially create a deck centralized around 2s right at the very beginning. This can help with playing into Wee Joker later tremendously, provided the player can find the Joker. Try copying a Death to convert cards into 2s, or The Hanged Man to get rid of many non-2s at once.

name: Wee Joker
text: Ghost Deck: Thanks to its easier access to Spectral cards, the Ghost Deck has great potential to manipulate the deck into being beneficial to Wee Joker. Try looking for Cryptid to create multiple new 2s, or Deja Vu to put a red seal on an existing 2.

name: Wee Joker
text: Abandoned Deck and Mad World Deck: Due to the small size of the deck, the likelihood of stumbling across 2s on these deck is very much better, and thus allows for more efficient scaling.

name: Wee Joker
text: 15 Minute City Deck is not recommended due to lack of 2s by default.

name: Wee Joker
text: As skipping is usually a high-risk strategy, it can be slightly tricky to win a run in 18 or fewer rounds, meaning the player must skip at least 6 Blinds, averaging at 1.25 Blinds per Ante skipped.

name: Wrathful Joker
text: Ghost Deck can find a Sigil Spectral card in the shop, which may convert cards into Spades.

name: Wrathful Joker
text: This Joker is easier to take with Checkered Deck, as the deck starts with 26 Spade playing cards.

name: Wrathful Joker
text: This Joker works best with Flush hands, if they contain only Spade suit cards. These hands are as follows:

text: Other hands that score more cards are generally better to play with Wrathful Joker, as they allow more Spade cards to be scored.

name: Wrathful Joker
text: As Wrathful Joker's effect triggers when a Spade card is scored, retrigger Jokers, that allow cards to be scored multiple times, are very good to combo with Wrathful.

name: Wrathful Joker
text: Flush Jokers, like Crafty Joker and Droll Joker, work well with Wrathful Joker, as you want to be playing flushes to maximize its effect anyways.

name: Wrathful Joker
text: Arrowhead also triggers off of Spade cards scored, forming a natural synergy with Wrathful Joker. As Arrowhead gives a large amount of Chips, Wrathful Joker's innate synergy with it is higher than other suit-Mult Jokers and their upgrades, as they boost both sides of the spectrum. name: Wrathful Joker
text: When facing The Goad, all Spade cards are debuffed, meaning Wrathful Joker cannot activate.

name: Yorick
text: Red Deck starts with an extra discard, which can help Yorick by allowing up to 5 more cards to be discarded than normally available.

name: Yorick
text: Painted Deck starts with a larger Hand size, letting the player get rid of unused cards to their heart's content while still being able to keep the important cards to form poker hands.

name: Yorick
text: Five-Card Draw Deck works very well with Yorick, as this deck starts with 6 discards, which means it can consistently gain X1 Mult every blind with the use of 5 discards.

name: Yorick
text: Golden Needle Deck may also work with Yorick, as this deck also starts with 6 discards. However, this deck penalizes the player by losing $1 for each discard, which can make it awkward to use Yorick.

name: Yorick
text: Yorick can be made to work with all poker hands. Discarding a large amount of cards to form bigger poker hands like Straight or Full House is a viable strategy, while smaller poker hands like High Card and Pair can still be made consistently after discarding for Yorick.

name: Yorick
text: Drunkard gives 1 extra discard, which is the same as using Red Deck, making scaling Yorick much easier.

name: Yorick
text: Merry Andy gives 3 extra discards, which drastically helps improving Yorick, almost always giving at least an extra X1 Mult to it every round if all discards are used to their maximum effect. Though, it is important to note that its downside, -1 Hand size, along with it being an Uncommon,
